The head of Bolivia’s judiciary has called for a Bolivia constituent assembly. Romer Saucedo Gomez leads the Supreme Tribunal of Justice.

He made the call in an interview with the agency EFE on 7 September. He was in New Delhi at a forum of BRICS supreme court presidents.

His words were an invitation rather than a demand. Let us open the Constitution, he said, and see what direction we give the country, with the whole country taking part.

He criticised the government’s preferred route of partial constitutional reform through the legislature. Excluding broad sectors, he warned, could produce social upheaval.

Why the Bolivia Constituent Assembly Call Lands Now

The immediate context is money. The judiciary is fighting the government over its share of the national budget.

The courts want their allocation raised from 0.35 percent to 5 percent. Legislators have proposed 3 percent.

A judiciary funded at a third of one percent of the budget is a weak branch by design. That is the argument behind the demand.

Calling for a constituent assembly raises the stakes from a line item to the constitutional order itself. That is a deliberate escalation.

What a Constituent Assembly Would Mean

Bolivia’s current Constitution dates from 2009 and came out of the last such process. It was the defining political project of the Morales era.

Reopening it would put the plurinational state, autonomy arrangements and judicial elections back on the table. Nothing in Bolivian politics is small once that door opens.

Saucedo’s alternative to it is the government’s partial reform through Congress. He argues that route leaves too many people out.

What We Could Not Establish

No response from the government of President Rodrigo Paz to this specific call could be sourced. That absence is itself worth recording.

There is an earlier exchange from 30 June, when a presidential spokesman called a threatened judicial strike unheard of. Saucedo replied that the magistrates have what the government lacks.

That was about the strike, not about the assembly. We do not present it as a reply to Sunday’s remarks.

The Other Bolivian Story This Week

President Paz decreed three days of national mourning on Monday 7 September. It follows two explosions at a military depot in Viacha, outside La Paz.

The blasts were on Friday 4 September at the Libertador Simon Bolivar regiment. The depot had stored black powder, mining explosives and pyrotechnics since 2019.

Nine people were killed and 81 injured, on Associated Press figures. The second explosion damaged homes up to two kilometres away.

Paz said the mourning is national but activities will not stop, with flags at half mast. The municipality of Viacha had declared its own three days of mourning on 5 September.

What to Watch

The first marker is whether the government answers. Ignoring a call from the head of the judiciary has its own cost.

The second is the budget vote. Three percent against five is the argument that produced this.

The third is whether other institutions join the call. One judge asking is a position, and a coalition asking is a process.

More: Latin America news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who called for a constituent assembly?

Romer Saucedo Gomez, president of Bolivia’s Supreme Tribunal of Justice, in an interview with EFE on 7 September 2026 while attending a forum of BRICS supreme court presidents in New Delhi.

What is the dispute behind it?

A budget fight. The judiciary wants its share of the national budget raised from 0.35 percent to 5 percent, against a legislative proposal of 3 percent. Saucedo also criticised the government’s preferred route of partial constitutional reform through Congress.

What happened at Viacha?

Two explosions at a military depot outside La Paz on Friday 4 September 2026 killed nine people and injured 81, on Associated Press figures. President Rodrigo Paz decreed three days of national mourning on 7 September.

World.title: Costa Rica Stops 4 Panama Gang Suspects at Border
World.content:
Four men linked by Costa Rican intelligence to Panamanian groups involved in drug trafficking and contract killing were stopped Saturday as they tried to enter by land at the southern border, the Public Security Ministry said. The ministry identified them only by the surnames Gutiérrez, Jiménez, Santoya and González. Officials said they are associated with two Panama-based organizations known as Los Terroristas de San Miguelito and Los Terroristas de Puerto Armuelles.

The southern land crossing is the Paso Canoas border between Costa Rica and Panama — the same route used by trucks, tourists, and, increasingly, by criminal networks moving people and cargo between the two countries. Vice Minister of Gobernación Omer Badilla said the stop was not a random checkpoint find. Intelligence had flagged the group before they reached the line.

“The now-detained individuals tried to enter the country this Saturday by land, at the southern border post. That intelligence allowed us to identify that these people would be linked to Panamanian criminal structures related to drug trafficking and sicariato,” Badilla said.The detention was a joint operation by the Directorate of Intelligence and National Security (DIS), the Border Police, and the Professional Migration Police.

The Public Security Ministry did not release first names, ages, or nationalities in its official account. It has been reported that the four men are Panamanian and said they will be deported. That nationality has not been confirmed in the ministry’s own statement.

What the government has said clearly is the next step which is once Costa Rica finishes coordination with Panama, the four will be handed over so they do not stay here in Costa Rican soil. “Costa Rica maintains a firm migration and security policy, based on intelligence, inter-institutional coordination and international cooperation, to prevent people linked to criminal structures from using our territory,” Badilla said.

San Miguelito is a dense district on the edge of Panama City that has long been one of that country’s homicide hot spots. Puerto Armuelles sits on Panama’s Pacific coast, close to the Costa Rican line and to the same South Pacific crossing that feeds Golfito, Pavones, and the Osa. Authorities on both sides of the border have spent the past two years describing that stretch as a transit zone for cocaine moving north and for hired gunmen moving with it.

Costa Rica has a reason to treat that traffic as more than a Panama problem. Homicides tied to trafficking groups have driven the murder totals in recent years, and the South Pacific and southern border have repeatedly shown up in OIJ cases involving Sicarios, stash sites, and clandestine airstrips. A large Caribbean cartel takedown earlier this year also documented landing strips built near the Panama border after a Coast Guard post in that area was closed in 2023.

This weekend’s stop does not, by itself, prove a new cell was about to set up in Costa Rica. It does show the government is now advertising the southern post as a filter, not just a customs gate. The ministry has not said whether the four men face charges in Costa Rica, whether weapons or cash were found, or whether Panama already had warrants on them. Those details will decide whether this is a one-day turnback or the opening of a joint case.

For those in the South Pacific area — or anyone crossing at Paso Canoas — keep in mind that for the time being at least, the land border is under an intelligence watch, and people flagged as part of known Panama hit crews are being pulled out of the incoming line rather than processed through and dealt with later. The four remain in Costa Rican custody pending the handover.

World.title: Man charged after neighbour spots stolen washing machine at repair shop; says he sold it for $25
World.content:
Man charged after neighbour spots stolen washing machine at repair shop; says he sold it for $25

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City man accused of stealing his neighbour’s $700 washing machine has pleaded not guilty after telling the court that the owner had actually given him the old machine because it was not working and he later sold it for just $25.

Richmond Isaac Roberts, 51, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on a charge of theft involving a blue-and-white Acros washing machine belonging to a 63-year-old neighbor.

Roberts initially attempted to plead guilty with an explanation, but after hearing the prosecution’s allegations, he disagreed.

“No, that dah nuh how it happened,” Roberts told the court.

He claimed the man had given him the washing machine because it was no longer working and that he subsequently sold it to another man for $25 for parts.

Based on that explanation, the Magistrate entered an equivocal plea of not guilty on Roberts’ behalf and offered him bail of $1,000 plus one surety of the same amount.

Roberts, however, was unable to immediately secure his release because court records showed he still had outstanding fines from previous matters, including a 2023 controlled-drug possession case, another theft matter and a 2015 bicycle offence for riding without a bell.

The court informed Roberts that the outstanding fines had to be settled before he could process bail. When he was unable to pay them, warrants were prepared for him to serve the default prison terms, leaving him behind bars at the Belize Central Prison.

In the current theft case, Bodden told police that on August 22 he left the washing machine beside the back step of his home before going to work. When he returned that evening, the machine was gone.

The man later spotted what he believed was his washing machine at a business that repairs refrigerators and appliances. He said the person there told him the machine had been obtained from Roberts.

The maintains that he never gave Roberts permission to take or sell the washing machine and told police it had been in working condition.

Roberts is now expected to challenge the theft allegation in court.

World.title: Two men challenge loitering charge after police bust them on Freetown Road; Man says he was working undercover security
World.content:
Two men challenge loitering charge after police bust them on Freetown Road; Man says he was working undercover security

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two Belize City men have pleaded not guilty to loitering after police accused them of remaining on Freetown Road despite being instructed to move along.

Roman Riverol, a security guard, and BTL software specialist Eli Elezor Obando appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where they were jointly charged with loitering in a public place.

Police allege the men were on Freetown Road and failed to move quietly along when instructed to do so by separate police officers.

Both men challenged the allegation.

Riverol told the court he was not simply hanging around the area but was working undercover security for a Chinese businessman whose store had reportedly been affected by increased criminal activity.

He said he was deliberately not wearing a security uniform so he would not easily be identified as the person guarding the establishment. Riverol claimed he explained the situation to police, but officers did not accept his explanation.

Obando, meanwhile, told the court he had only been speaking with Riverol when police arrived. He said he initially left the area but later returned and was detained when police came back and found him there again.

Both men pleaded not guilty and were granted self-bail of $100 each.

They are due back in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on October 5, 2026.

The Magistrate reportedly warned both men of the consequences of failing to return to court, as self-bail is less commonly granted than bail secured through a surety.

World.title: Corozal businessman slapped with $94,015 in fines after massive illegal seafood bust
World.content:
Corozal businessman slapped with $94,015 in fines after massive illegal seafood bust

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Corozal businessman has been slapped with more than $94,000 in fines after pleading guilty to illegally importing hundreds of pounds of jumbo shrimp and tilapia fillets along with octopus into Belize.

Leslie Lizarraga, 34, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court alongside 51-year-old David Romano Arana of Consejo Village following a Fisheries Department operation on September 3.

Lizarraga pleaded guilty to three counts of illegal importation and was fined a total of $94,015, while Arana pleaded not guilty and the prosecution subsequently withdrew all three charges against him.

The case arose after Fisheries officers, assisted by police, intercepted a silver GMC Sierra pickup along the Hattieville-Boom Road following a brief pursuit.

Authorities say the vehicle initially turned around and sped away from officers before eventually losing control and ending up in a ditch.

A search reportedly uncovered seven boxes containing 335 pounds of jumbo shrimp, another 58 boxes containing 1,566 tilapia fillets weighing approximately 290 pounds, and a bag containing 14 pieces of octopus.

The Fisheries Department had previously confirmed the seizure, saying the seafood was suspected of having been illegally imported and that both the vehicle and products were taken into its custody. The department warned that unauthorized seafood imports can present food safety and phytosanitary risks and undermine legitimate businesses that comply with Belize’s import requirements.

After seeking a sentencing indication from the court, Lizarraga’s attorney, David McKoy, entered guilty pleas on his client’s behalf. The court took into account that Lizarraga was a first-time offender and had saved judicial time by pleading guilty, opting for fines rather than imprisonment.

Lizarraga was fined $5,000 for illegally importing the shrimp, another $5,000 for the tilapia and $5,000 for the octopus, along with court costs.

The heaviest penalty came from the 1,566 tilapia fillets, for which an additional fine of $50 per piece amounted to $78,300. The 14 pieces of octopus attracted a further $700 penalty.

The prosecution also applied for the forfeiture of the GMC Sierra used to transport the seafood. McKoy objected, telling the court that the pickup does not belong to Lizarraga and arguing that its owner must be given an opportunity to oppose its forfeiture.

The Magistrate agreed to adjourn the forfeiture application until the vehicle’s owner can be notified and heard. The pickup remains in Fisheries Department custody.

Fisheries officials have since said their intelligence indicates illegally imported seafood has been moving into Belize regularly and supplying businesses including resorts and supermarkets. The department says investigators are also tracing potential buyers of the illegal products.

World.title: Joseph Vaccaro committed to stand trial for Gaston Barrow murder after challenging witness evidence
World.content:
Joseph Vaccaro committed to stand trial for Gaston Barrow murder after challenging witness evidence

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Belize City taxi operator Joseph Gabourel Vaccaro has been committed to stand trial in the High Court for the 2025 murder of Gaston Barrow, despite telling the Chief Magistrate that three prosecution witnesses did not identify him as the shooter.

Vaccaro, 31, appeared unrepresented in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Monday for the conclusion of his preliminary inquiry, nearly a year after he was remanded on the murder charge.

During the hearing, the prosecution submitted more than 70 statements and other documentary evidence, including photographs, DVDs, chain-of-custody forms, warrants and a wanted poster.

Vaccaro challenged portions of the prosecution’s evidence, telling the court that three witnesses whose statements were included in the disclosure did not name him as the person who fired the fatal shots. He questioned why he was being prosecuted for murder if those witnesses had not identified him as the shooter.

The Chief Magistrate explained that the Magistrate’s Court was not conducting the murder trial and that Vaccaro would have the opportunity to challenge the prosecution’s evidence when the matter is heard before the High Court.

The matter ended in a paper committal, and Vaccaro was ordered to stand trial during the High Court session beginning October 7, 2026.

Vaccaro was originally arraigned on October 6, 2025 and remanded to the Belize Central Prison. In July, he received 154 pages of disclosure along with five CDs and photographs forming part of the prosecution’s case.

The charge stems from the September 28, 2025 shooting at the Old Belize compound along the George Price Highway.

Police said Barrow was travelling in the front passenger seat of a vehicle driven by Hance Card, with two women in the rear, when a gunman allegedly approached from the vicinity of a taxi and opened fire.

Barrow was fatally wounded, while Card was also shot but survived. Police later said Card declined to provide investigators with a statement.

Investigators reviewed surveillance footage from the Old Belize compound, which police said eventually led them to Vaccaro. Public reporting at the time said police believed the attack was gang-related and possibly connected to retaliatory violence.

Vaccaro remains on remand awaiting his High Court trial.

World.title: Nearly 400 police officers, undercover cops and drones deployed for Carnival; about 12 detained
World.content:
Nearly 400 police officers, undercover cops and drones deployed for Carnival; about 12 detained

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nearly 400 police officers were deployed for Saturday’s Belize City Carnival Road March as authorities used uniformed officers, undercover personnel, drones and Coast Guard support to police the massive event.

ASP Stacy Smith said major events such as Carnival require advance operational planning because of the large crowds and the possibility that individuals may use those gatherings to target rivals.

Just under 400 officers were strategically deployed, including uniformed personnel, members of specialized operational units and undercover Special Branch officers.

Smith joked that some undercover personnel may even have been dressed in Carnival costumes.

Police also deployed drones along the route, which Smith said allowed officers to identify and intervene in disturbances before they escalated.

About 12 people were detained in connection with various disturbances, but police say the event generally concluded without any major security incident.

The Belize Coast Guard also assisted police because portions of the Carnival activity took place near the seafront.

The 2026 Road March began at Lord Rhaburn Plaza at Memorial Park and ended at the Marion Jones Sporting Complex.

Smith thanked the officers who worked the event as well as members of the public who cooperated with authorities.

World.title: Police say no extra officers deployed to Cayo despite drug tensions; technology and intelligence driving operations
World.content:
Police say no extra officers deployed to Cayo despite drug tensions; technology and intelligence driving operations

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department says it has not deployed additional officers to Western Belize in response to recent drug-related violence, arguing that sustained operations and increased use of technology are already underway in the area.

ASP Stacy Smith said police have been concentrating operational resources in Cayo for some time and believe recent successes are partly the result of investment in technology and intelligence-led policing.

Police have previously linked violence in San Ignacio and Santa Elena to competition over the illegal drug trade and have said cocaine and crack cocaine are increasingly appearing among younger users and street-level dealers.

Last week, police reported that operations in Cayo had removed more than 35,000 grams of cannabis, 2,468 grams of cocaine, 1,253 grams of crack cocaine and 1,043 grams of methamphetamine from the streets. Police said those operations resulted in dozens of people being charged.

Smith said authorities remain interested in targeting major suppliers but stressed that street-level dealers are also part of the trafficking network.

She argued that disrupting retail sellers reduces the local market and, in turn, the incentive for larger quantities of drugs to enter the country.

Smith also noted that drugs do not only enter Belize by illicit aircraft, pointing to Belize’s land borders with Guatemala and Mexico. Police continue to use the Mobile Interdiction Unit in northern and western Belize to target suspected trafficking routes.

Two of five new pickup trucks recently provided to the Police Department have also been assigned to the Cayo District.

World.title: Police identify vehicle type in Brianna Myvett murder but still have no motive or suspects
World.content:
Police identify vehicle type in Brianna Myvett murder but still have no motive or suspects

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police say surveillance footage has helped investigators identify the make and model of a vehicle believed to have been involved in the murder of 20-year-old Brianna Myvett, but the vehicle did not carry licence plates and no motive has yet been established.

Myvett was shot and killed on Freetown Road on the night of August 31 while she was inside a Ford Escape with 24-year-old Alexander Carr, who was also shot and injured. Public reports described Myvett as a recent Wesley Junior College graduate, volleyball player and employee of the Belize Central Prison.

ASP Stacy Smith said investigators have retrieved several pieces of video footage and have been tracing the vehicle of interest in an effort to determine who entered or occupied it.

Two persons of interest were detained based on statements investigators received concerning a possible motive, but Smith said that line of investigation has so far yielded nothing concrete.

Police say neither Myvett nor Carr was known to police, and investigators have not determined whether Myvett, Carr or both were the intended targets.

“No motive has been established,” Smith said, adding that police are continuing to commit resources to the investigation.

Myvett was laid to rest on September 2.

World.title: NIP issued to pickup driver after Red Bank motorcycle crash kills 59-year-old man
World.content:
NIP issued to pickup driver after Red Bank motorcycle crash kills 59-year-old man

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have issued a Notice of Intended Prosecution to a female pickup driver following a fatal traffic accident in Red Bank Village that claimed the life of 59-year-old Nerry Campbell.

The collision occurred at about 10:45 a.m. on Saturday, September 5.

Police say Campbell was travelling on a motorcycle and was turning onto the Red Bank Road when a collision occurred with a pickup truck.

Campbell sustained serious injuries and was taken for medical treatment but succumbed shortly after 1:00 p.m.

Public reporting identified Campbell as a Guatemalan labourer living in Red Bank Village and identified the pickup as a Toyota Tundra driven by 30-year-old Deidra Jackson of Silk Grass. The collision reportedly occurred at the junction of Red Bank Road and the Thomas Vincent Ramos Highway.

Police have since issued Jackson a Notice of Intended Prosecution as the investigation continues.

World.title: Rough start
World.content:
Grade two students at Holland Primary School seated during their outdoor class under a bamboo structure on Monday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

THE education ministry on Monday reported a generally smooth reopening of schools across the island for the start of the 2026/27 academic year but principals, mostly in hurricane-ravaged western Jamaica, highlighted a raft of difficulties.

Among the complaints were incomplete repairs as well as classes held in heat-trapping tents that turn into sweltering ovens under the tropical sun.

“Based on preliminary data received from all seven educational regions covering approximately 1,000 schools, only three schools did not open today, meaning that approximately 99.7 per cent of the schools captured in the data were able to open on the first day of the new school year,” the ministry said in a news release.

While the ministry said late furniture delivery was among the most frequently reported challenges on Monday, Jamaica Observer journalists received first-hand reports of the rough start to the academic year in the sections of the island that suffered the brunt of Hurricane Melissa’s fury last October.

Stories on Pages 3 to 10.

World.title: Two traditions, one future
World.content:
Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon (centre), along with former Hydel High Principal Dr Walton Small (right), as well as teachers and students of the newly merged Hydel Cumberland High School, release balloons in celebration of the official opening of the merged institution on the first day of the new academic year, Monday. (Photos: Garfield Robinson)

EDUCATION Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon officially unveiled the newly merged Hydel Cumberland High School Monday, declaring that the unification wasn’t about erasing either school’s identity, but rather combining the best of their traditions to create a single learning environment better equipped to serve students and make fuller use of existing resources.

“I love to see the new motto: ‘On the wings of excellence, endeavour to soar.’ And that’s a merger of the two mottos of the two schools. So even starting with the name, we merged the two schools. With the motto, we have merged the two schools and their ethos,” Morris Dixon said Monday while delivering greetings at the name unveiling ceremony at the school’s campus in Portmore, St Catherine.

As she helped to officiate both the historic first day of the school and the start of the 2026-2027 academic year, Morris Dixon explained that Cumberland High School had a capacity for 1,200 students but had only been operating with just over 300 students when she visited about a year ago. She added that the infrastructural challenges at Hydel High, coupled with Cumberland’s available space, made the merger a practical option.

“One of the things we had thought about was potentially moving the children in little groups to different schools, putting them all around St Catherine. But I think this is the best option. I think this was quite strategic in nature, and that’s how we’re going to continue to do this restructuring of education in Jamaica — be strategic — because now that we have one institution instead of two, it means we can direct more resources to one… that is our plan,” said Morris Dixon.

Already, significant investment is being made in the new school. The minister announced that $70 million is being spent to improve its electrical system while work is also being done on the home economics laboratory.

She added that the school’s parking lot will be expanded to accommodate the increased number of staff, while upgrades to the sporting facilities are also planned.

“So there’s a lot that will happen here, and Principal [Carlon Pitt] can ask for everything he wants. Principal, we’ve already granted your first wish, which was more students, but your success, the success of this merged institution, is really important to the Ministry of Education. We are very much committed to it. We’re committed to seeing the traditions work together and to achieve so much more,” she said.

Morris Dixon acknowledged, however, that bringing together two established school communities would not be without challenges but promised that her ministry would be strongly supporting the school’s leadership to smoothly navigate any trials that may arise.

“There are understandable emotions when schools merge. I know there is sadness from some who are, you know, leaving a space that they’re used to. There are those who are seeing all these new children come and these new teachers come. There are a lot of emotions involved in this, and so I want to acknowledge those emotions. Change is never easy; it’s always hard. And us adults, we sometimes have a harder time than the children with change,” she said.

“So teachers, I know this is an emotional period for you… I know that you’re great, I know you’re wonderful, I have no doubt that we have the best teachers in this world in Jamaica, so I know we can get through this. The ministry is here to support, in whatever way we can, to the students who may be coming to this new environment. You have a good principal, you have a good team here; you’re going to be okay,” Morris Dixon assured.

Principal Pitt told the Jamaica Observer that as the former head of Cumberland High he was highly receptive to the idea of a school merger.

Welcoming this new chapter in his career, Pitt emphasised that his vision focuses heavily on academics while prioritising students’ holistic development.

Highlighting Cumberland’s status as a leading Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution in St Catherine, alongside Hydel’s strong culture of sports and academics, the principal noted that the merger offers the perfect opportunity to fulfill his goals.

“Whatever we do in school, it must result in student outcome, the students must be the biggest beneficiary of whatever we do. And so the primary focus is on adding value, value-added education, adding value to the students with respect to their starting point and where they exit. So far we have added more sciences to the curriculum. We have now the traditional sixth form… we have a sports programme to roll out that we are excited about, and so with all of these things it is about the holistic development of the child,” Pitt said.

World.title: Jahshii to embark on islandwide tour; aims to reconnect with his fans
World.content:
JAHSHII...the fanbase a grow and mi just waa continue grow with the fans.

IN a move to reconnect with his fan base, dancehall artiste Jahshii is set to embark on a multi-stop tour across the island in November.

The Born Fighter artiste says the tour will feature performances backed by Tower Band and he’s also bringing along some special guests at each stop.

“The fanbase a grow and mi just waa continue grow with the fans,” he told the Jamaica Observer recently.

“The islandwide tour will kick off in November, and you can expect high-energy performances, special guests at each stop. We’ll be going across the island, and it will be a live music experience like no other,” Jahshii assured.

He added, “We really want to get the fans dem closer, like in an up close and personal vibe, so we have been doing rehearsals while locking in the venues.”

Jahshii, who is best known for songs like Pieces featuring Masicka, Cream of the Crop and

Born Fighter, revealed that it wasn’t an easy journey to get to where he is today.

“Mi a come from nobody naw do nuttin fi mi; a fight wi fight to get up deh. But it is very satisfying to help other emerging talent and see how they develop and make it in the music,” he shared.

Father to a young son, Jahshii says fatherhood has changed his perspective on life.

“It has changed my outlook on life; family comes first and my priorities come first. That’s what we get from being a father,” he shared.

Jahshii’s latest single Auto Pilot, produced by Troublemekka, was released two months ago. He says new music is on the way.

“We definitely have some new music coming especially for the ladies, because we not leaving them out,” he said.

World.title: CPL Hall of Fame award named in honour of Sir Garfield Sobers
World.content:
Garfield Sobers

BRIDGETOWN, Barbados (CMC) — The Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) has announced that the trophy presented to each year’s player inducted into its hall of fame will be officially named the Sir Garry Sobers Award, in tribute to the man universally recognised as the greatest all-rounder West Indies cricket has ever produced.

The naming follows the recent launch of the CPL Hall of Fame which will honour two inductees annually, one player and one off-field contributor.

Dwayne Bravo and Ian Bishop were confirmed as the inaugural class, and the CPL has now secured the Sobers family’s blessing to attach Sir Garry’s name to the award, marking one of the most significant moments in the league’s history.

As one of the finest cricketers the game has ever seen and a defining figure of West Indies cricket, Sir Garry’s name gives prestige to the Hall of Fame recognition.

The Sir Garry Sobers Award will be presented for the first time at the CPL Hall of Fame Gala Dinner on September 15, 2026 at the Hilton Barbados.

The evening is being held in support of the Sir Clive Lloyd Healthcare Foundation’s prostate cancer awareness, testing, and early detection work across the Caribbean.

With the trophy carrying Sir Garry’s name the gala brings together two of West Indies cricket’s most respected figures for a single showpiece night in support of the region.

Pete Russell, CEO of CPL, said “Sir Garry Sobers was, without question, the greatest all-rounder the game has ever seen, and having his name on this award means a great deal to everyone at CPL. We are enormously grateful to the Sobers family for trusting us with his name and his legacy. It gives this trophy, and this hall of fame, a weight our players will carry with real pride. To present it for the first time at a gala dinner in support of Sir Clive Lloyd’s Healthcare Foundation makes 15 September an even more prestigious night for West Indies cricket.”

World.title: ‘SPOILT KIDS’
World.content:
RICKETTS... FIFA has supported us and I’ll be very ungrateful not to show some regard, and show some respect, and say thanks to a man that has supported Caribbean football (Photo: Observer file)

JAMAICA Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts has come to the defence of FIFA President Gianni Infantino, saying he doesn’t deserve the treatment he’s receiving from stakeholders. Ricketts also labeled UEFA “spoilt kids” for its stance against the FIFA boss.

On Sunday, football’s world governing body confirmed that Infantino intends to stand again in next year’s elections for a fourth term, despite mounting criticism over recent months. Infantino proposed selling stakes in FIFA competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to private investors and offered FIFA’s 211 member associations US$40 million ($6.3 billion) each if they backed the plan.

However, the 56-year-old Swiss ultimately scrapped it following widespread opposition, including European football governing body, UEFA, who voted to boycott all World Cups if it went ahead. Concacaf, who governs North America and the Caribbean, also rejected the proposal.

Infantino, though, attempted to smooth things over with several Concacaf members after attending a Caribbean Football Union (CFU) Presidents’ Meeting and the CFU Under-14 series in the Dominican Republic last month, where Jamaica reached the final. Concacaf President and FIFA Vice-President Victor Montagliani had written to Infantino, asking him not to attend.

Reports from England stated many of the Concacaf members were “infuriated” by Infantino’s behaviour.

However, while not providing the details of the meeting, Ricketts told the Jamaica Observer that the FIFA boss was treated with the utmost respect.

“That’s how reporting and that’s how media is — some people try to sensationalise certain events to suit their own agenda — but that’s the farthest thing from the truth,” he said. “I think Infantino was warmly, warmly welcomed; he was embraced by almost every single CFU member.”

Ricketts, who has served as JFF boss for nearly a decade, admits that Infantino should have approached the proposal differently, although he had no issue with its premise.

“Infantino might have made a mistake, but the intentions were to help Caribbean countries or help smaller countries. Can you imagine Jamaica getting 40 million US dollars to invest in football? Can you imagine the difference that would make in four or five years?” said Ricketts.

“In my very first utterance, I did say that the gesture would suit me but we thought [there] was [a] lack of communication, lack of discussions, it seemed non-transparent. But I don’t think Infantino meant to hurt anybody or would have tried to make himself a beneficiary of the gesture.”

The fallout from the proposal continues Belgium Football Association, on Monday, the latest to oppose Infantino’s re-election. At least 11 other FIFA member associations have publicly withdrawn their support including major European football nations such as England, Germany, Norway and the Netherlands.

UEFA has led calls for Infantino to step down and is preparing legal action against him, accusing the FIFA president of “criminal mismanagement” over the proposal. FIFA, in return, has accused the Euopean governing body of a “smear campaign against it and its leadership”.

Ricketts believes UEFA are being unreasonable and has no intention of following its stance.

“People will have different views and different opinions for different reasons. But I am not supporting UEFA because I think that they always want to be in opposition and always want to oppose. It doesn’t matter who is president, they are going to have issues. It doesn’t matter how well the president does, they are going to have issues and I think that UEFA is behaving like a set of spoilt kids,” he said.

“From a commercial standpoint, they really don’t need FIFA. They probably have as much money as FIFA does so they can do and say anything. I can’t do that because I need support and FIFA has supported us and I’ll be very ungrateful not to show some regard and show some respect and say thanks to a man that has supported Caribbean football.”

More than 20 FIFA member associations, including 2026 World Cup finalists Argentina, World Cup co-host Mexico and African champions Morocco, have publicly expressed support for Infantino .

Ricketts praised Infantino’s performance but says the decision on Jamaica’s support for rests with the JFF board.

“This is something I probably don’t even have the right to speak on because it’s a decision that the board will have to make. But personally, I think Infantino has done a good job,” he said.

The nominations for FIFA presidential candidates must be submitted by November 18. Infantino is currently the only candidate, though Concacaf President Victor Montagliani is being touted as a potential challenger.

World.title: Wedding, Fashion & Interior Design
World.content:
Inspired by the beautifully curated spaces they encounter worldwide, couples are choosing venues like boutique hotels to evoke those same unforgettable feelings on their wedding day. -

New York Fashion Week is upon us, and it got me thinking about how much fashion and interior design influence the wedding industry. We often look at weddings as their own creative world, but they are actually incredibly responsive to what is happening around us. What we wear, how we decorate our homes, the restaurants and hotels we are drawn to, even the way luxury brands present themselves all eventually find their way into weddings.

And increasingly, I think the most interesting weddings are borrowing ideas rather than following wedding trends.

The Runway Has Always Found Its Way to the Aisle

Fashion is perhaps the most obvious influence. What happens on the runways of New York, Paris, Milan and London eventually changes what brides and grooms want to wear, but its influence goes much further than the dress.

The current fashion conversation is full of personality: sculptural silhouettes, interesting textures, dramatic draping, bows, metallics, sheer fabrics, unexpected colour and a renewed appreciation for beautiful tailoring. Those ideas translate remarkably well into weddings.

A beautifully draped fashion silhouette can inspire the treatment of a tent. A couture floral appliqué can become the starting point for an invitation, cake or tablescape. A runway colour combination can suddenly make traditional wedding palettes feel completely different.

Even bridal fashion itself has become less formulaic. Brides are changing looks throughout the celebration, experimenting with shorter dresses, statement accessories, dramatic veils and fashion-forward reception looks. Grooms, too, are embracing more colour, texture and individuality.

Weddings Are Beginning to Look More Like Beautiful Interiors

Interior design is having an even greater influence on weddings.

For years, wedding décor was largely about flowers, linens and centrepieces. Couples are paying attention to chairs, lamps, rugs, bars, shelving, interesting furniture, textured fabrics and architectural details. The lounge is no longer simply somewhere to put a sofa; it can feel like the living room of an incredibly stylish home. Bars are becoming statement pieces. Dinner spaces are layered with lighting and objects in much the same way an interior designer would style a room.

I particularly love the move towards residential-style lighting. Table lamps, shaded pendants and warm pools of light immediately change the feeling of a wedding. They make large spaces feel intimate and give outdoor celebrations a sense of permanence and warmth.

This is where I think the influence of boutique hotels, restaurants and private members’ clubs has become especially important. Couples travel. They dine out. They experience beautifully designed spaces around the world, and naturally they want their celebrations to evoke some of those same feelings.

They may not say, “I want an interior-designed wedding.” They say, “I want it to feel like this hotel in Paris,” or “I loved this restaurant in New York.” That distinction matters.

The New Luxury Is Atmosphere

I think we will continue to see couples becoming more confident about mixing influences — vintage furniture with contemporary florals, fashion-inspired fabrics with traditional tablescapes, chrome against soft linen, sculptural pieces beside organic greenery.

The objective isn’t necessarily for everything to “match.” It is for everything to belong to the same story.

Fashion Is Also Teaching Weddings to Be More Personal

Perhaps my favourite influence from fashion is individuality. For a long time, weddings came with an unwritten formula of what was considered “bridal”. White, blush, certain flowers, certain chairs, certain stationery, certain photographs. That vocabulary has expanded enormously.

Today’s couple can create a wedding that is minimalist, maximalist, tropical, editorial, romantic, architectural, vintage, fashion-forward or wonderfully difficult to categorise.

Looking Beyond the Wedding Industry

As New York Fashion Week begins, I’ll certainly be watching the clothes, but I’ll also be looking at the sets, colour combinations, fabrics, styling and tiny details that make a collection memorable.

Because inspiration doesn’t always arrive labelled “wedding.”

Sometimes it is a handbag. A hotel lobby. A fashion show. A restaurant in another country. A fabric you can’t stop touching. A beautifully designed room. A colour combination you would never have thought to put together.

The best wedding professionals know how to notice those things, reinterpret them and make them relevant to the couple, the location and the celebration. For me, that is where wedding design becomes most exciting.

The future of weddings isn’t simply about following the next wedding trend. It is about looking at the wider world of design, fashion, travel and culture — and asking: how can we turn that inspiration into something that feels entirely our own?

Shikima Hinds

Managing Director

Shikima Hinds Events Concierge

Tel. 876-925-4285 or 876-361-0910

Email: shikima@shikimahinds.com

www.shikimahinds.com

World.title: Documentary on James Bond creator Ian Fleming to premiere at GoldenEye
World.content:
Portrait taken in the early 1960s of Ian Fleming, a British journalist, secret service agent, writer, whose most famous creation was the superhero James Bond, agent 007. (Photo: AFP)

Ian Fleming and the Curse of James Bond, directed by Adam Low, a new feature documentary exploring the life, imagination and enduring legacy of James Bond creator Ian Fleming, will premiere at GoldenEye, Fleming’s former Jamaican home, during the 80th anniversary year of the villa’s construction.

The documentary explores Fleming beyond the legend of 007, considering the contradictions, pressures and fascinations that shaped both the man and the charged literary world he created, according to a press release by Gross Media, which executive produced the project.

Presented at GoldenEye by Gross Media, the premiere weekend – November 19 to November 22, 2026 – brings together biography, place and mythology in a setting deeply connected to the Bond story.

“GoldenEye’s enduring legacy as a center of Jamaican art and creativity is rare and compelling,” said Gross Media founder David M Gross. “So much new has originated here and radiated outward — through music, painting, literature and the performing arts. Our film invites a new generation to come to Oracabessa, St Mary, to understand that legacy and be inspired by it.”

Built in a uniquely Jamaican architectural style, the iconic villa features whitewashed walls, wooden louvers and has no glass windowpanes.

Upon returning from espionage duties during World War II, Fleming built the villa in 1946 on Jamaica’s famed North Coast. GoldenEye became the creative sanctuary where he wrote each of the 12 James Bond nov els and the stories that introduced one of the most recognizable characters in modern popular culture.

Eight decades later, the property remains a living landmark: part legendary literary site, part cultural myth and an enduring symbol of Jamaica’s oversized place in the Bond story and the wider cultural world.

“Fleming built GoldenEye as a place where he could write, and every James Bond novel was written here. Eighty years later, it remains the spiritual birthplace of Bond. To screen a film that looks so closely at Fleming himself, during GoldenEye’s 80th year, is very special,” said Chris Blackwell, Founder, and Marika Kessler, CEO, Island Outpost.

Adam Low, the film’s director, said he was “determined to put Jamaica at the centre of the story” with the project.

“Even the Bond books not set there are infused with the island’s atmosphere, landscape and history. By including Jamaican voices — from Fleming’s longtime gardener Ramsay Dacosta to novelist Marlon James as well as Minister Olivia ‘Babsy’ Grange whose relative Aunt Violet was Fleming’s house manager — the film shows how deeply Jamaica shaped Fleming’s imagination and the world of Bond,” Low said.

“As Minister Grange says in the film, ‘Jamaica is the star of the Bond films,’ and the documentary makes a compelling case that without Jamaica, there would be no James Bond,” said Low, underlining the Jamaican connection.

The perspective of the film deepens the premiere’s connection to GoldenEye by positioning Jamaica not simply as Fleming’s retreat, but as a defining creative force behind Bond’s settings, sensibility and mythology.

“By weaving together Jamaican voices, landscapes and history, the documentary underscores the island’s central place in both Fleming’s imagination and the continuing cultural life of 007,” said film editor Joanna Crickmay.

According to the release, the film’s opening sequence features a moving benediction in the Rastafari tradition by author, journalist and cultural liaison Barbara Blake-Hannah, while driving the vibrant streets through Oracabessa, St Mary, en route to GoldenEye with Desmond Dekker & The Aces’ legendary rocksteady and reggae track “007 (Shanty Town)” on play.

The premiere film weekend will bring guests from around the world to the place where Fleming’s daily writing ritual helped launch the Bond phenomenon, the release stated, adding that the programme includes a screening at PlayScape, a cocktail party at the GoldenEye villa with a Jamaican jazz band, a classic Jamaican BBQ on Button Beach with members of the film’s crew and Ian Fleming-themed morning breakfasts: scrambled eggs, toast, guava jelly, local fruits and Blue Mountain coffee.

Together, the events offer guests a rare opportunity to experience the film in the setting most closely associated with Fleming’s creative life, according to the press release.

World.title: Stronger schools
World.content:
Education Minster Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon walks with students of Maud McLeod High School in Westmoreland where she filmed her back-to-school message to the nation.

After a school year battered by Hurricane Melissa, particularly in western Jamaica, but capped by improved results in the country’s major examinations, Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon is looking to the new school year with optimism, pointing to increased investment, and stronger infrastructure as Jamaica pushes to transform its education system.

The scale of the challenge facing schools remains stark.

According to Morris Dixon’s back-to-school message, more than 688 schools were damaged by Melissa, 313 of them severely, while almost $26 billion is being spent on repairs and reconstruction. As she has repeatedly done in the past few weeks she acknowledged, however, that the work is not advancing as quickly as the Government would like.

Still, she said preparations were being made to get schools open, including contingency arrangements for institutions where repairs have not yet been completed.

“Thanks to the excellent work of our principals, boards, and the ministry team, we are working to have all schools open tomorrow. I have to thank all who have worked so hard over the summer and who have put in place contingency plans to support reopening even where repairs are not completed,” she said.

For Morris Dixon, however, rebuilding after Melissa is only part of the task.

The Government is entering the new school year with more than $835 million in operational support for schools, representing an average 55 per cent increase in funding. The minister said all schools received the first tranche of the increased funding in June, ahead of the reopening.

More than $1 billion is also being invested in educational resources, including workbooks, readers, textbooks, e-books, virtual learning solutions, and supplementary materials.

The increased spending comes against the backdrop of what Morris Dixon described as a strong finish to the last academic year, despite the disruption caused by the Category 5 storm.

“Despite the historic, once-in- a- 100-year devastation caused by the passage of Hurricane Melissa, we ended the last academic year with improved results across our major exams — PEP, CSEC and CAPE. Jamaica’s children did so well despite so much being thrown at them!” she said.

The minister is now betting on that resilience, alongside new investments, to drive further gains. In her speech she reminded the country of plans already in place.

Among the biggest initiatives is a $400-million investment in technical and vocational education at high schools. Technical high schools are to receive state-of-the-art laboratories in areas including autonomous robotics, renewable energy, virtual welding, electrical engineering, industrial controls, and optoelectronics.

The Government is also retooling science laboratories, while more than 150 satellite systems have been distributed to schools to improve Internet access, with additional devices being procured, particularly for rural institutions.

Morris Dixon said the hurricane recovery programme is similarly being used as an opportunity to improve schools beyond simply repairing the damage.

“Our Melissa reconstruction programme has not only presented an opportunity to make our schools more resilient, but it has also provided an opportunity to upgrade and renovate staffrooms for educators across Jamaica. The Staffroom Renovation Programme covers 74 institutions in the first phase, with work concentrated heavily in the parishes hardest hit by Melissa,” she said.

And while buildings, equipment and technology are central to the push, the minister also highlighted the needs of students outside the classroom.

More than 160,000 students are projected to benefit from the traditional cooked lunch programme, while another 69,000 students in the most challenged schools are expected to receive both breakfast and lunch. Meanwhile, 316 school cooks were trained and received range cook certification over the summer.

Psychosocial and psychological support, including trauma-informed services and Psychological First Aid, will also continue into the new academic year, after being intensified during the previous one.

Morris Dixon said the ambition extends beyond simply getting schools reopened and students back into classrooms.

“The ministry’s commitment is to continue transforming education so that every child, regardless of where they live or their circumstances, has a fair opportunity to learn, grow and succeed,” she said.

World.title: France and Canada join UK in issuing trade sanctions on Israeli settlements
World.content:
LONDON — France and Canada will join the U.K. in imposing new trade sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements Tuesday in a major diplomatic coup for Britain as it resets its relationship with Israel.

In the House of Commons, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confirmed Britain, France and Canada will impose a ban on the trade of goods and some services from Israeli settlements, having last month condemned Israel’s plans for 1,200 new homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem.

The U.K. “will take action against specific companies and individuals who provide services such as construction, infrastructure, financing, or real estate for settlement expansion,” Miliband told MPs, adding: “To those who finance or facilitate illegal settlements, let me say this, you will face the full force of UK sanctions.”

World.title: France calls for new EU taxes to raise €60B
World.content:
There are lingering concerns that a bad budget deal for France could boost the far-right National Rally, which is ahead in the polls and has campaigned to halve Paris’ contributions to the EU budget.

During a closed-door discussion on Tuesday, France’s ambassador to the EU, Philippe Léglise-Costa, told colleagues that new EU-wide levies should generate over €60 billion — a high threshold for most other countries, according to the diplomats, who have direct knowledge of the talks. None of the other countries specified how much money they want to generate through the new taxes.

While most governments support introducing new own resources, they have misgivings about the specific ideas on the table.

The European Commission’s proposal from last July envisaged five new levies that would generate up to €66 billion in extra revenue. But the package has been met with resistance from national governments.

The Irish Council presidency, which is steering discussions on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), aims to narrow down the number of own resources that are acceptable for EU countries during a leaders’ summit in Brussels on Oct. 15.

Dublin on Monday hailed “consensus” among governments to introduce new levies on foreign polluters, known as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and electronic waste that could respectively generate €1.64 billion and €17.9 billion per year on average from 2028 to 2034.

During Tuesday's discussion, the Commission opened the door to tweaking some of the tax proposals to generate more revenue than initially foreseen, one of the diplomats said.

But in a significant blow for France, other tax proposals — targeting tobacco products, corporate turnover and revenues from the Emissions Trading Scheme — have faced opposition from several countries, according to a note from Ireland seen by POLITICO.

World.title: Ursula von der Leyen condemns ‘shocking’ Ratko Mladić funeral in Serbia
World.content:
Mladić was the commander of the Bosnian Serb Army during the 1992-95 Bosnian War and was found responsible for the Srebrenica genocide, in which more than 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys were killed in July 1995.

The Serbian government said that it had no hand in organizing the funeral, however Mladić’s body was flown to Serbia on a government plane and his coffin was escorted by members of the Serbian Armed Forces.

“The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable,” von der Leyen said, adding that “they demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe’s recent history.”

“The images from Ratko Mladić’s funeral yesterday in Belgrade were shocking,” wrote European Council President António Costa. “Ratko Mladić was a convicted war criminal. He was responsible for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.”

Serbia, which is an EU candidate country, has not opened a new negotiating chapter with the bloc since December 2021. The process is blocked by eight member countries over its rule-of-law record and its refusal to sanction Russia for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

World.title: EU court rules in favor of Ikea against Belgian far-right party
World.content:
The firm sued Vlaams Belang in Belgium in November 2022, alleging trademark law infringement. The Belgian business court then asked the CJEU for its advice on how to strike the balance between freedom of expression and the right of a business to defend its trademark.

“It does not appear that the use of the Ikea trade marks for the sole purpose of taking advantage of their reputation to reinforce a political message … takes precedence over the rights and interests” of the Swedish brand, the CJEU said in its press release about the verdict.

The fact that Vlaams Belang’s campaign was completely unrelated to Ikea’s business — and that people may have believed that the company had endorsed it — weighed into the ruling, said Elena Izyumenko, assistant professor in intellectual property law at Amsterdam’s Institute for Information Law.

“What the court suggests is that a private company can suppress controversial political expression if it can create any impression of a link between the company and the opinion expressed in the parody,” Izyumenko said.

The case will now return to the Belgian court, which will rely on the CJEU’s interpretation of the law to issue its ruling. Looking at the CJEU’s ruling, “It’s almost obvious that it will rule against Vlaams Belang,” Izyumenko said.

“The non-profit organization Vrijheidsfonds of Vlaams Belang takes note of the ruling of the European Court of Justice and will thoroughly examine its scope in the context of further legal proceedings,” a spokesperson for the party said.

Ikea did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

World.title: Hindu group’s Eiffel Tower visit sparks uproar after female staff sidelined
World.content:
According to staff representatives, female employees were told to step aside so as not to be seen by the group during the visit. Staff went on strike Monday to protest the move, forcing the monument to close.

Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire, a member of the center-left Socialist Party, said on X that “gender equality will never stop at the foot of our historic monuments, nor anywhere else in this city. It must apply everywhere, for everyone.”

Marine Le Pen, the far-right front-runner in next year’s presidential election, stressed that “in France, we will never accept the presence of women being ‘limited.’”

Aurore Bergé, the minister for gender equality and a member of French President Emmanuel Macron’s centrist party Renaissance, called the incident “unacceptable.”

“In France, no religion is above the law,” she said.

The BAPS delegation was in Paris as part of a two-week-long celebration inauguration of its first branch in France. Modi called the event “a matter of great joy.”

On X, the French BAPS branch said that “to the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower” while “sincerely [apologizing] for any pain or inconvenience caused.”

“We believe in the universal values of mutual respect and service,” it added.

World.title: US escalates ahead of UK trade sanctions on Israeli settlements
World.content:
Huckabee’s comments came after Florida Congressman Randy Fine warned on X that sanctions would effectively “ban any British company forced to comply from doing business with any state or local government in Florida” under state law.

The diplomat’s comments will unnerve British exporters, who are already navigating an increasingly fragile trading relationship with the U.S.

Speaking at an awards ceremony in Jerusalem on Tuesday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog said the imposition of trade sanctions on Israeli settlements would prove to be a "grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history,” according to a readout of the comments provided by Herzog's office.

In a post on X written in Spanish, Israel’s Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the far-right Jewish Power party, said Israel should recognize the Falkland Islands as Argentine territory under occupation, which the British violently stole from the Argentine people.

The U.K. retained its control of the Falklands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas, after a 74-day war following Argentina's invasion of the territory in 1982.

'Comprehensive reset'

Miliband's expected announcement, and promise of “comprehensive reset” of policy on Israel, marks a sharp shift in Britain's stance on Israeli settlements under new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.



It comes just two weeks before Burnham's expected trip to New York for the U.N. General Assembly — and a potential first in-person meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump.

World.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv resume after pause for Witkoff and Kushner visit
World.content:
Moscow and Kyiv had paused their attacks on each other as U.S. special envoys traveled to both capitals for talks over the weekend.

At least 12 people were killed overnight Monday into Tuesday in the first Russian airstrikes on Kyiv since the three-day ceasefire prompted by the visit of U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, authorities in the capital said.

Administrative buildings, warehouses, schools and residential buildings were damaged in six districts of Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported. At least 10 people were injured.

The overnight attack extended beyond the Ukrainian capital to the Odesa region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it "a complex strike" that "tried to plan to cause as much harm to life as possible."

World.title: Inside Burnham’s big Israel gamble
World.content:
Britain is about to take its toughest stance yet against Israel – but will it make a difference, or will it leave the UK isolated on the international stage?

Andy Burnham and Ed Miliband will unveil a package of sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the West Bank, putting Britain at the forefront of the G7’s effort to pressure Benjamin Netanyahu’s government.

Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy examine what the move means in practice – and why the government has chosen to act now.

But with tensions rising, will the move impact the UK’s relationship with the United States and Israel?

Plus, after a turbulent conference, has Reform UK seen a bounce in the polls, and could it give an early indication of the direction of travel for the Holborn and St Pancras by-election?

World.title: Breakfast at noon? Turns out weekend meals at random times can hurt men’s hearts
World.content:
Do you eat breakfast at lunchtime and dinner at a time when you’d normally be sleeping during weekends? This inconsistency is what researchers call “eating jet lag” and it might be hurting men’s – you read it right, only men’s – hearts.

 

Early work or school starts often force people to adjust their eating schedules during the week, which differs from meal times on weekends and days off.

Such a shift in eating patterns may disrupt the body’s biological rhythms and could have implications for cardiovascular health, according to a new French study. Each additional hour of “eating jet lag” increased the risk of cardiovascular disease by 14% and the risk of coronary heart disease by 21% among men, researchers found.

“This study suggests the importance of regular meal-timing patterns, beyond sleep and diet quality, in cardiovascular disease prevention,” the authors wrote.

The research, published in Communications Medicine, analysed the timing of more than 100,000 participants' first and last meals on working days and on weekends over a 14-year follow-up period between 2009 and 2023.

Men are more affected

Participants were classified by their eating schedules: the first group ate meals earlier on the weekends than during the week, the second group kept similar schedules across both and the last group had their meals later at weekends.

Both groups that ate either later or earlier than usual faced a higher cardiovascular risk than the regular group, regardless of overall diet quality.

Surprisingly, this pattern was only found among men, and women did not appear to be affected by schedule changes.

Why?

One reason could be that men generally have a higher absolute risk of cardiovascular disease. The authors also noted that women tend to be more inclined towards morning routines than men, a difference linked to variations in anatomy and hormones, which may influence how their bodies respond to shifts in meal timing.

What’s behind the irregular meal timings?

The authors’ leading theory for why this happens is that eating jet lag increases the risk of cardiovascular events through circadian disruption.

Circadian rhythms are the body’s internal clocks, running on a 24-hour cycle that help regulate its functioning. They are mainly regulated by light, but eating patterns can also act as a synchroniser for peripheral clocks, such as those in the liver and heart. Aligning eating patterns with these internal rhythms boosts metabolic health, while inconsistency can disrupt the body’s internal balance.

The authors noted that if the results are confirmed by further large-scale studies, meal timing regularity could become a key focus for interventions to reduce chronic disease risk and ease public health burdens.

World.title: European Parliament's report tightens EU investment conditions as China negotiations heat up
World.content:
Three MEPs have agreed in a report to be published Wednesday to tighten the requirements for foreign direct investment in the EU, restricting access to the European market for Chinese investors, Euronews has learned.

 

The report comes from the European Parliament’s rapporteurs on the proposed Industrial Accelerator Act, MEPs Christophe Grudler (Renew), Pierre Jouvet (S&D) and MEP Anna Cavazzini (The Greens). The act was presented by the European Commission last March and creates a European preference on the EU market to favour products made in Europe, in a move to protect strategic sectors of EU industry from foreign competition.

However, China has threatened several times to retaliate against the legislation, which is still under discussion, putting access to the EU market at the top of the agenda in some ongoing trade negotiations with Brussels.

The exclusive details of the report obtained by Euronews show that in sectors where China is dominant, among them electric vehicles, solar panels, critical raw materials and batteries, the three rapporteurs want to impose strict requirements on investments exceeding €50 million, a threshold lower than the €100 million initially proposed by the Commission.

For such investments, any investor from a country holding 40% of the sector’s global market share will have to meet six conditions: own no more than 49% of the share capital of the EU target; make the investment through a joint venture with an EU entity; transfer technologies to Europeans; ensure that at least 60% of the workforce consists of EU workers; reinvest at least 1% of annual revenue into research and development within the EU; and source at least 30% of manufacturing inputs from within the bloc.

A signal to Beijing

The rapporteurs have added to the Commission’s proposal investments in other sectors such as wind power, electrolysers and heat pumps, making it necessary for the investor to meet at least three of the conditions above.

The report also restricts access to public procurement and public support schemes to products made in the 27 EU member states.

The Commission will only be allowed to extend the scope to products coming from non-EU countries under strict conditions, such as the application of reciprocal access for Europeans to foreign countries’ public procurement.

This follows intense lobbying from EU foreign partners, which want their products to be recognised as “made in Europe” to access the EU market. Many, such as the United Kingdom, argued that EU value chains were too intertwined with their own market to exclude them.

The report by the three MEPs will now have to be adopted by EU lawmakers before discussions start with EU member states on this future legislation.

However, it sends a signal to China that Europeans will not give up in their attempt to protect the EU market from China’s aggressive industrial policy.

World.title: Zelenskyy expects Trump meeting in late September as Kyiv pushes for air defence and new talks
World.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday he expects to meet his US counterpart Donald Trump by the end of September, as Washington steps up efforts to revive negotiations to end Russia’s full-scale invasion.

 

Zelenskyy said securing additional US air-defence missiles would be a key issue at the meeting, with Kyiv seeking an urgently needed “winter package” of anti-ballistic missile interceptors.

Speaking to reporters in the presidential WhatsApp chat, Zelenskyy said he discussed Ukraine’s shortage of advanced air defences with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner during their visit to Kyiv over the weekend.

“I am counting on a meeting...with President Trump, raising this issue and, God willing, there will be a result,” Zelenskyy said.

The Ukrainian president said Kyiv explained to Witkoff and Kushner in detail what it needed from a US “winter package” and when the weapons would be required.

“We talked with Witkoff and Kushner about the shortage that we have, which we feel regarding the winter package, a package of anti-ballistic missiles,” he said.

“Until we have this result, we need ballistic missile packages from the Americans. They heard in detail what we need and when we need it.”

US President Donald Trump meets with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara, 8 July, 2026 AP Photo

Zelenskyy also said Ukraine was moving towards a new trilateral negotiating format with the United States and Russia, although he declined to disclose details of the preparations.

“We are also moving, in my view, towards a trilateral format,” he said. “Here I cannot disclose all the details. We agreed with the American side: let us prepare all of this between ourselves first and then communicate it to the public.”

The United Arab Emirates, Switzerland and Turkey are among the possible locations for such a meeting, Zelenskyy said, adding that several countries had offered to host talks.

He said energy infrastructure and grain exports could form part of prospective talks with Russia, alongside humanitarian issues, particularly prisoner-of-war exchanges.

“We need not only to discuss (these issue), but to have a concrete result,” Zelenskyy said.

Europe ‘will be’ in future negotiations

Zelenskyy also sought to make clear that renewed US-led diplomacy would not exclude Kyiv’s European allies from negotiations.

He said European diplomats maintained their own contacts with Russia, stressing that Washington was not the only channel of communication with Moscow.

“Let’s be honest: they are thinking about the security of all of Europe,” Zelenskyy said of European governments.

“That is why it is clear that they must be at the table in any format of negotiations.”

He also pointed to Ukraine’s prospective EU membership, post-war reconstruction and future security guarantees as areas in which European involvement would remain essential.

European representatives already took part in the latest talks in Kyiv alongside the US delegation, he said, adding that Europe would be involved in all future negotiating formats.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and European representatives in Kyiv, 6 September, 2026 AP Photo

Patriot licences and the winter shortage

Alongside diplomacy, Zelenskyy said Kyiv was continuing direct negotiations with Trump over licences for the production of Patriot missiles, as Ukraine seeks a longer-term answer to its dependence on US supplies.

He said talks were taking place both between the Ukrainian and US teams and at manufacturer level, and that Trump had responded positively, although Kyiv was seeking to accelerate the process.

For now, however, Ukraine’s immediate concern is securing enough interceptors to protect the country through the coming winter.

Zelenskyy said he had told Ukraine’s partners that a winter air-defence package was now Kyiv’s priority.

Britain on Tuesday announced a €116mn contribution to Ukraine’s winter air-defence package, including support for Patriot missiles, as well as other air-defence interceptors, artillery ammunition and drones. The equipment is due to be delivered before winter through NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List programme.

Zelenskyy spoke as Russia launched another attack on Kyiv, with a drone striking a television station while journalists were live on air.

The building was partially destroyed and at least five people were reported injured, according to Zelenskyy. Emergency workers extinguished a fire at the site, while authorities warned that the number of casualties could rise.

“‘Shaheds’ against the media mark a new chapter in Russia’s degradation and Europe and the world must certainly respond to this,” Zelenskyy said.

“Not a single strike against Ukraine and Ukrainians - against life itself - can be left unpunished. Russia must be stopped and this is possible only through joint efforts.”

World.title: Serbia and Uzbekistan target more trade as President Mirziyoyev visits Belgrade
World.content:
Serbia and Uzbekistan held the first meeting of their Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation in Belgrade on Monday, hours before Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev was due to arrive for a two-day official visit.

 

The meeting brought together Serbian Minister Nenad Popović, responsible for international economic cooperation, and Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov.

As Euronews Serbia reported, the talks focused on increasing trade and investment, connecting companies more directly and identifying sectors for joint projects.

Bilateral trade reached about $41.9m (€36.1m) in 2025, a record for the two countries. Serbian Chamber of Commerce figures put the increase at 27% compared with 2024, when trade was worth $32.9m. Serbian exports accounted for $26.39m of last year’s total, while imports from Uzbekistan reached $15.46m.

“Our task is to turn this strong political momentum into concrete results: increased trade, new investments, joint projects, and a stronger presence of Serbian companies on the Uzbek market,” Popović said.

Officials from Serbia and Uzbekistan meet in Belgrade for the first session of the Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation. Euronews Serbia

Agriculture leads the expansion

Agriculture and food production are emerging as two of the fastest-growing parts of the relationship.

Serbian exports of agricultural and food products to Uzbekistan rose by 54.1% between January and July 2026, according to figures presented at the meeting.

Officials identified seeds and planting material, agricultural machinery and food-processing equipment as areas where further growth could be possible.

But the two governments are looking well beyond agriculture.

The sectors discussed include mechanical and electrical engineering, pharmaceuticals, textiles, construction, energy, transport and logistics, as well as information technology, artificial intelligence, robotics and digitalisation.

At the end of Monday’s meeting, Popović and Kudratov signed a protocol setting out priority areas and future steps. The two sides also agreed that the commission would become the main institutional mechanism for following up agreements and developing new economic initiatives.

Free trade talks on the table

One of the potentially more consequential steps is the prospect of a bilateral free trade agreement.

“We are also beginning talks on a free trade agreement, which, together with duty-free trade, would lead to increased trade in goods,” Kudratov said.

The idea predates Mirziyoyev’s visit. Serbian and Uzbek officials had already discussed launching negotiations on a free trade agreement during talks in Tashkent in May.

For both sides, the objective is to move beyond a bilateral trade relationship that remains small compared with the size of their economies.

Uzbek economic officials have argued that Serbia could provide Uzbek companies with a gateway to Central and Southeast European markets, while closer ties with Uzbekistan would give Serbian firms greater access to one of Central Asia’s largest markets.

Mirziyoyev visit adds political momentum

The commission met shortly before Mirziyoyev’s arrival in Belgrade, where he is due to hold talks with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić.

The Uzbek presidency said the visit would focus on trade, investment and joint projects in transport, mechanical engineering, light and food industries, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and information technology. Organised labour migration is also on the agenda.

On Tuesday, the two presidents are scheduled to sign a joint statement establishing a strategic partnership between Serbia and Uzbekistan, alongside a broader package of bilateral documents. A Serbia-Uzbekistan business forum is also planned in Belgrade.

The visit follows Vučić’s trip to Uzbekistan in October 2025 and comes as Serbia prepares to open an embassy in Tashkent, another sign of the rapid expansion of political contacts between the two countries.

For Belgrade, the relationship also has a political dimension: Serbian officials have repeatedly highlighted Uzbekistan’s support for Serbia’s territorial integrity and its position on Kosovo.

World.title: Can dogs sniff out cancer? Indian start-up turns their noses to AI
World.content:
At a research centre outside Bengaluru, 15 trained dogs are being taught to identify cancer-related odours in human breath samples.

 

The dogs wear customised helmets and harnesses fitted with sensors that record their breathing, brain activity and movements as they sniff.

Artificial intelligence then analyses the data to identify patterns in the animals' responses.

Company reports 90% accuracy

Dognosis says a recent study involving more than 1,500 participants across six hospitals found an accuracy rate of more than 90% across seven types of cancer.
