World.title: Breaking: Hungary orders 10 Russian embassy staff to leave – UPDATE: Russia’s threat
World.content:
Hungary has ordered 10 employees of the Russian Embassy in Budapest to leave the country, saying their activities were incompatible with the conduct expected of diplomats under the Vienna Convention. A spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry said Budapest should expect a “harsh and painful response”.

FM Orbán announces letting go of 10 embassy employees

Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced the decision, describing it as unprecedented in scale. She said the relevant official at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had informed Russia’s ambassador to Budapest of the decision on her instructions. According to Orbán, the Hungarian authorities assessed that the 10 representatives had engaged in activities that were not acceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention.

“The decision protects Hungary’s security and sovereignty,” the minister said. She stressed, however, that the move does not mean a break in diplomatic relations with the Kremlin. Hungary intends to maintain the necessary dialogue with Moscow, provided that both sides respect one another and comply with international rules.

UPDATE: Russia’s threat

Russia will respond to Hungary’s expulsion of ten Russian diplomats, according to the Russian state news agency TASS, citing a statement from the Russian Foreign Ministry. Maria Zakharova, spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry, promised a “harsh and painful response.”

“The response to the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful,” she told TASS.

A tougher approach towards Moscow

The expulsions mark a notably tougher public response towards Russian diplomatic activity than previous measures taken by Hungary. Péter Magyar also raised the announcement in Parliament, reading out Orbán’s statement and saying that a Tisza government would protect Hungary’s sovereignty, reports Telex.

Anita Orbán has adopted a more distant diplomatic approach towards Russia than her predecessor, Péter Szijjártó, according to the supplied sources. On 13 May, shortly after taking office, she summoned Russia’s ambassador following a Russian drone attack against Transcarpathia. Szijjártó had last summoned a Russian diplomat in February 2022. The latest move also follows reports of a quieter expulsion of a Russian intelligence officer earlier this year.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Kremlin intelligence officer reportedly expelled in May

VSquare reported in May that Artur Sushkov, allegedly a Russian intelligence officer operating under diplomatic cover at the Embassy in Budapest, left Hungary on 4 May. According to the report, Hungary’s Constitutional Protection Office had established that Sushkov had spent years collecting information on institutions close to the Hungarian government. VSquare’s government sources claimed that Hungarian intelligence had recommended his expulsion as early as February, but that the previous Orbán government had blocked the proposal.

Stay up-to-date: FM Anita Orbán reports progress on minority rights for Hungarians in Ukraine

2018 Skripal case provides a different precedent

Hungary also expelled a Russian diplomat in 2018 following the poisoning of former Kremlin intelligence officer Sergei Skripal in Britain. However, a subsequent Direkt36 investigation suggested that Budapest deliberately handled the expulsion in a way that would minimise damage to its close relationship with Moscow.

Diplomatic sources reportedly said the expelled Russian was a GRU military intelligence officer whose posting was due to end within months. The latest decision is considerably larger in scale, as the 10 embassy employees have now been ordered to leave Hungary. Despite this, Budapest insists that diplomatic relations with Moscow will continue, with the government presenting the expulsions as a measure to protect Hungary’s security and sovereignty rather than a move towards severing ties with Russia.

Read also: Putin adviser claims Ukraine could lose Transcarpathia, calls Western Ukraine a ‘den of evil’

World.title: Hungary launches major new rural development programme: 100 villages to test new model
World.content:
Hungary’s government has launched the Saint Stephen Rural Development Programme, a new initiative aimed at strengthening rural communities and giving local residents a greater say over how development funding is spent. The pilot phase will cover 10 rural micro-regions, 100 settlements and nearly 100,000 people. If the model proves successful, it could be rolled out nationwide from 20 August 2027, potentially reaching more than 2,100 settlements and 1.8 million people.

The new programme starts in 10 regions

Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced the launch of the Saint Stephen Rural Development Programme (Szent István vidékfejlesztési program) in Parliament on Tuesday. The initiative will initially be tested in 10 rural micro-regions, covering around 100 settlements and nearly 100,000 residents.

The selected areas are:

Zalakaros and its surrounding area

Harkány and its region

Bács

Pásztó

Medgyesegyháza

Igal

Tiszaújváros

Gyöngyös

Nyírbátor

Gönc and its surrounding area

According to the government, the areas were selected using indicators including average per-capita income subject to personal income tax and a complex development index. The average per-capita income in the participating regions is HUF 308,629, which is 36.7% below the national average.

Another important development programme launched by the Magyar government: Hungary set to launch EUR 5.5 billion railway upgrade as development plan gets green light

HUF 1 billion for every 10 settlements

One of the programme’s most significant commitments is a HUF 1 billion annual community development fund for every group of 10 settlements. However, the government says the initiative is not simply about providing additional money. A key principle is that decisions about how the funding is used should be made locally rather than imposed from Budapest.

The 10 settlements in each participating area will be expected to work together to identify their most pressing needs and development opportunities. Local residents and experts will then assess the problems and potential of the area, draw up a joint development strategy and prepare investment plans that are both professionally sound and financially realistic.

In other words, the central government is promising to provide the funding, while local communities will have a much stronger say in deciding what the money should be used for.

Keeping young people in rural Hungary

One of the central objectives of the programme is to make rural areas more attractive places to live, work and raise a family. Magyar argued that it is not enough to simply tell young people to stay in their hometowns.

If there are no jobs, nurseries or adequate public services nearby, roads are in poor condition, or internet access is inadequate, young people may have little realistic choice but to move away. The government therefore wants to create rural communities where staying is a genuine choice rather than a necessity or sacrifice.

The programme could support improvements to local infrastructure, services, businesses and economic opportunities, although the exact projects will ultimately depend on the needs identified by each participating community.

Why does rural depopulation matter?

Many smaller Hungarian settlements have faced a combination of population decline, the departure of younger residents and shrinking access to local services. Magyar highlighted the potential chain reaction: young people leave, schools and shops close, employment opportunities become scarcer, businesses find it harder to operate and essential services become increasingly difficult to access.

Eventually, a community may no longer be asking how it can develop, but how it can simply survive. The Saint Stephen Programme is intended to reverse this trend by strengthening the population-retaining capacity of rural areas. The idea is not simply to preserve villages as they are, but to give them the economic and social conditions needed to offer residents a viable future.

What happens after the pilot?

The first phase is explicitly a pilot programme. Over the coming months, residents, local authorities and experts will work together to assess the challenges and opportunities in the 10 selected regions.

They will then develop local strategies and identify concrete investment projects. The government plans to evaluate the results of the pilot before deciding on the next stage. If the model works, it could form the basis of a nationwide rural and regional development network.

The government says that national implementation could begin after 20 August 2027. At that stage, the programme could potentially cover around 2,174 rural settlements and approximately 1.85 million people.

Major changes could also be coming to county assemblies

The announcement of the rural development programme was accompanied by another major proposal: the government is working on legislation that would abolish Hungary’s county assemblies in their current form and fundamentally restructure the system.

Magyar strongly criticised the existing county assemblies, arguing that they have become largely detached from meaningful regional development. He also accused opposition parties of using the institutions as political and financial patronage networks.

The government has already abolished expense allowances for county assembly presidents and vice-presidents and reduced the previously paid salaries of assembly leaders. According to Magyar, restructuring the system could free up additional public funds that could instead be channelled into development projects.

The exact form of the proposed new system remains unclear, however, and further details are expected when the government’s legislation is presented.

Photo: Pixabay

How is the programme different from existing rural initiatives?

The Saint Stephen Programme is not being introduced as a replacement for every existing rural development measure. Magyar said it would operate alongside the Hungarian Village Programme and the Competitive Districts Programme. Its distinctive feature is the emphasis on local decision-making.

Rather than having central authorities determine what a village needs and then asking local governments to fit their plans into an existing funding scheme, the new approach aims to start with the communities themselves. The government’s message is essentially: local people know their communities best, so they should have a greater role in deciding their future.

A major test for Hungary’s new rural policy

The Saint Stephen Programme represents an ambitious attempt to change the way rural development is organised in Hungary. But for now, it remains to be seen how effectively the model will work in practice.

The first 10 regions will provide an important test: can neighbouring settlements agree on shared priorities? Can local residents meaningfully influence investment decisions? And can the available funding generate improvements that make rural communities more attractive to young families and businesses?

If the pilot delivers the results the government expects, the programme could enter a much larger phase from 2027. That would bring the initiative from 100 settlements to more than 2,100, potentially affecting almost two million people.

World.title: Video: Two 14-year-olds arrested after fire-setting and vandalism at Hungarian school
World.content:
Two teenagers have been identified and detained after setting fire to rubbish, damaging trees and throwing stones at a surveillance camera outside a secondary school in Polgár, eastern Hungary. Police reportedly identified the suspects within just 24 hours.

The incident caused widespread outrage in the town after security camera footage captured the youths vandalising the public space in front of the local secondary school.

Camera footage captured the vandalism

Polgár Mayor József Tóth first reported the incident on social media in an unusually angry post, expressing his frustration over the destruction of trees, shrubs and flowers that had been carefully maintained throughout the hot and unusually dry summer.

The town’s surveillance cameras recorded two young people tearing out newly planted trees before apparently setting fire to rubbish in the public area. They also threw stones at one of the cameras, according to the footage released by the mayor. The damage came despite the municipality’s efforts to keep the area in good condition throughout the summer heat and lack of rainfall.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Police identified the suspects within a day

The vandalism prompted an immediate police investigation. According to HAON, officers in Hajdú-Bihar County identified the suspected perpetrators within 24 hours. The suspects are reportedly two 14-year-old boys.

The mayor subsequently shared a photograph of one of the minors on social media, describing the youths as having disregarded the basic rules of community life and calling for them to face the legal consequences of their actions. “In addition to legal accountability, his actions should result in public condemnation and contempt,” he added.

At the same time, his comments prompted a discussion about how communities should respond to serious vandalism committed by minors, particularly when public property and potentially dangerous acts such as fire-setting are involved.

The case has attracted considerable attention locally, with residents expressing anger over the destruction of public greenery and the apparent attempt to damage the town’s surveillance system. The investigation will determine the exact circumstances of the incident and what legal consequences the two teenagers may face.

World.title: PM Magyar: “Hungarians turned against Hungarians” in the past 16 years
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar told Parliament on Monday that over the past 16 years Hungarians had turned against Hungarians and “those who took an oath to serve the Hungarian people plundered the country”.

“The previous regime unleashed destruction”

He said the previous regime had unleashed such destruction that it left behind parched land, hospital wards at 40°C, trains with flaming wheels, and humiliated teachers, “as if a foreign army had marched through the country”.

While Hungarian families fought for survival, he said, the former political “mafia” leader, Viktor Orbán, had built “a private estate out of our labour and our tax forints”.

Magyar began his speech by thanking Speaker of Parliament Agnes Forsthoffer for assuming the responsibilities of the president of the republic in the interim.

He also thanked the viewers of public news channel M1, noting that after more than a decade, parliamentary proceedings had returned to public media airwaves. “Viewers can now hear the truth firsthand,” he said.

Magyar said the Hungarian people had often experienced devastation from external forces throughout their history. “That is why the betrayal committed by the governments of Viktor Orbán against Hungary over the past decades is unforgivable, because they did not attack us as a foreign army under foreign flags,” he declared.

He said the previous regime had unleashed such destruction that it left behind parched land, hospital wards at 40°C, trains with flaming wheels, and humiliated teachers, “as if a foreign army had marched through the country”. While Hungarian families fought for survival, he said, the former political “mafia” leader, Viktor Orbán, had built “a private estate out of our labour and our tax forints”.

Photo: MTI

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

“Denying responsibility amounts to complicity with the past”

Regarding the responsibility of previous governments, Magyar warned that denying responsibility amounted to complicity with the past, and that delivering justice was the most fundamental moral condition for laying new foundations. “And we will not be complicit,” he declared.

Referring to the former ruling parties, Fidesz and the Christian Democrats, Magyar said that a “solid future” could not be built as long as the “perpetrators” sitting in parliament tried to evade responsibility.

He thanked voters for the mandate they gave him on 12 April and said people had begun turning to each other again, with less hatred and more joy, with families no longer turning away from each other because of partisan politics. “Once again, we are thinking and acting as one united nation for Hungary,” Magyar said.

If you missed it: Magyar government targets thousands of billions in Orbán-era private equity deals

The prime minister said that by the spring of 2026, the state had “basically ceased to function” in areas such as railway services, hospitals, water management and schools. “The state gave up its most fundamental tasks: protecting its citizens and their dignity,” he added.

Magyar thanked nurses, teachers, police officers, firefighters, social workers, child protection and water management staff, as well as government officials, who, “despite the Orbán regime’s destructiveness, carried the country on their shoulders for years, trying to ease the consequences of the previous government’s ineptitude”.

Photo: MTI

Normal state operations “cannot be built on exploitation of public employees”

He pledged to build a state in which those people “do not need to take a daily exam of heroism and self-sacrifice”, arguing that the operations of a normal state “cannot be built on the exploitation of those working in the public sector”.

However, Magyar asked public sector workers for patience, citing the “extremely difficult” budget situation caused by “emptied coffers and amassed debt”. He said the government’s room for manoeuvre was severely restricted. “We have to fight for each forint, and we will do so,” he added.

Magyar said that there was no more uplifting mission than “restoring Hungary from the ruins,” while calling it “infinitely sad how little our predecessors loved the country”. “Anyone who truly loves their nation would never, not for a single moment, allow rural hospitals to fall into disrepair, leave Hungarian soil parched, or view their own people as mere subjects to be exploited while stuffing private estates with wealth stolen from the nation,” he added.

He said the government’s determination to act stemmed from this deep outrage, driving them to pull the country back from the “edge of the abyss” and begin “laying the foundations of a new fortress system”.

Magyar noted that the Tisza government had ended rule by decree and removed “the puppets of the Orbán regime” from their positions. He accused the former ruling parties of planning to lose the election while ensuring they never truly lost power. “We did not come here to assist those who covered up the plundering of the nation in any way, no matter where the political mafia placed them. We have no business with them,” he said.

The prime minister said they had negotiated the “historic” agreement with the European Union in just three weeks, whereas their predecessors “spent years merely blackmailing, vetoing and fighting a pointless battle on the international stage”, while denying Hungarian families access to their own lawfully due funds.

Photo: MTI

The government fully meets all conditions required to unlock EU funds

By 31 August, the government had fully met all the conditions it had committed to — despite every attempt to prevent it — thanks to thousands of well-prepared diplomats, lawyers and government officials working day and night, who showed the world what Hungarian expertise and professional dedication are capable of when they are finally given a clear goal and genuine appreciation by their government, he said.

Magyar said funds recovered would be used to renew public transport, develop the electricity grid and energy storage, modernise hospitals and primary care, support home renovations, Hungarian SMEs, research, innovation, digitalisation in education, and water management and environmental projects.

He noted the government had cut ministers’ and state secretaries’ pay and party group allowances and was now discussing a radical cut in the prime minister’s salary. Magyar noted that in July, the Hungarian budget had produced a surplus unseen for decades.

A National Asset Recovery and Protection Office has been set up “so that the fate of every stolen forint can be revealed”, he said, adding that the dissolution of 16 public-interest asset management foundations had returned over one trillion forints in public assets to the state. This included 845 billion forints in corporate stakes, 162 billion forints in cash, nearly 90 billion forints in securities and about 88 billion forints in real estate, he said.

Photo: MTI

Public media “freed” from “party propaganda”

The prime minister said the public media had been freed from “party propaganda” and expressed his satisfaction that parliamentary sessions could again be followed on the M1 news channel.

Magyar said the minimum old-age pension would be raised to 120,000 forints, benefits for people with changed work capacity would be restored, a 100,000-forint school-start allowance would be introduced, the price of firewood would be cut by 5 percent and resources for social firewood frameworks would be doubled, and VAT on prescription drugs scrapped.

He said there had been critical weeks this summer when the country had had to fight for its sheer physical functioning, in reference to problems at the Paks nuclear power plant, and he thanked Hungarian families and businesses for curbing their consumption. He outlined measures taken to protect the plant and said that in the coming weeks, permanent technical protection would be built at Paks.

“For us, this is what a functioning Hungary means,” he said, adding: “We do not shirk responsibility, we do not paralyse ourselves, we do not make excuses, we assess the situation, we decide and we act.”

The government was building a functioning rule-of-law state with clear steps, and would review and transform concessions, Magyar said.

“We will take back what we can”

He stressed that they faced a historic task: laying new, rock-solid institutional foundations. They would start where money had been flowing unchecked into private pockets for years, and in the coming weeks, they would review and likely completely transform the tobacco, casino, waste and motorway concessions, he said, adding that the billions in profits would then enrich the community, the budget and Hungarian taxpayers instead of “private oligarchs”.

“From what the Orbán regime cynically siphoned off over the decades, we will take back what we can, renegotiate where necessary, while filling the state administration with qualified experts,” he said.

Regarding the protection of natural treasures, the prime minister spoke of tightening environmental fines, setting up the National Environmental Inspectorate, submitting a new climate law to parliament and launching a national afforestation programme.

In health care, Magyar highlighted the publication of hospital infection data hidden for years, reducing waiting lists, launching a hospital cooling programme, renewing the financing of GP practices and restoring the dignity of the midwife network.

New budget to begin wage adjustments

He said the new budget to be submitted in mid-October would begin wage adjustments for those in education, social and child protection work, law enforcement and national defence. A stricter child protection law would be adopted and a national drug strategy launched, he added.

The prime minister said they would put a roof over the heads of those guaranteed affordable housing by the housing law, launch the “Your homeland awaits” programme to bring back talent forced abroad, restore freedom in research and develop a modern higher education strategy. A large-scale main and secondary road renovation programme would be launched, railways would be developed and “stolen” local government autonomy would be returned to settlements, he said.

Magyar said order would also be restored in the world of bailiffs, notaries and liquidators.

World.title: FM Anita Orbán reports progress on minority rights for Hungarians in Ukraine
World.content:
Hungary says progress has been made in securing minority rights for the Hungarian community in Ukraine’s Transcarpathia region, with Kyiv beginning preparations for the legislation needed to implement previous commitments.

Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said on Monday that the latest developments marked a step forward in efforts to protect the rights of ethnic Hungarians in Transcarpathia. She said she had spoken three times with Hungary’s consul general in Uzhhorod over the previous 48 hours, as Ukraine’s education ministry had begun preparing the necessary legislation.

Hungary and Ukraine resume minority talks

Orbán recalled that minority rights consultations between Hungary and Ukraine resumed on 20 May. Since then, she said, the two sides had secured concrete commitments from Kyiv. Under the agreement, Ukraine has pledged to incorporate the minority rights discussed during the negotiations into national legislation.

According to Orbán, the first tangible result has already emerged. Following a decision by the Ukrainian government on 15 July, the network of small educational institutions will be preserved from 1 September, while their state funding will also continue.

The issue is particularly significant for Hungary’s community in Transcarpathia, where access to education in the Hungarian language has been a long-standing concern.

EU also links minority plan to talks

Hungary has also sought to ensure that Ukraine’s obligations are reflected at EU level. At Hungary’s initiative, the European Union has stipulated that Ukraine’s minority action plan must be brought into line with the results of the Hungarian-Ukrainian negotiations, Orbán said.

“This is now about implementation, and both sides are working on it,” the minister wrote.

Hungary and Ukraine have recently been putting effort into addressing longstanding disputes over the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia. Budapest has repeatedly called for guarantees concerning education, language use and other minority rights, while Kyiv has been seeking closer integration with the European Union.

World.title: Orbán’s Fidesz demands EU ‘immediately release’ all funds owed to Hungary
World.content:
Fidesz MEPs are demanding the European Union immediately and unconditionally release billions of euros in funding for Hungary, while also calling for more money for border protection and agriculture.

The Fidesz-KDNP group in the European Parliament has called for the immediate and unconditional payment of all EU funds allocated to Hungary, arguing that money negotiated by Viktor Orbán’s government has been withheld for political reasons.

In a statement sent to Hungary’s state news agency MTI on Monday, the group said it wanted the EU’s 2027 budget increased by EUR 11 billion. Tamás Deutsch, a Fidesz MEP and member of the European Parliament’s Budget Committee, submitted the proposal on behalf of the Hungarian delegation.

Fidesz demands billions in frozen EU funds

According to Fidesz, around 55% of the funding under three Hungarian operational programmes – approximately EUR 6.3 billion – was frozen in 2022 for political reasons. The party is now demanding that not only the post-pandemic recovery funds but also Hungary’s entire cohesion funding allocation be paid without conditions.

Fidesz stressed that an Orbán-led delegation negotiated EUR 22 billion in cohesion funding for Hungary in December 2020, in addition to the EU’s recovery fund. The party claims that part of this money has subsequently been withheld by the European Commission and what it called the European Parliament’s “liberal majority”.

The statement also called for a EUR 2.5 billion increase in the Common Agricultural Policy budget, with additional support for young farmers, the wine sector and beekeepers.

If you missed it: Here comes the twist: could Fidesz and Mi Hazánk be heading for a merger?

More EU money for border protection

The Hungarian delegation within the European Parliament’s Patriots group is also seeking major changes to EU spending on migration. It wants EUR 1 billion removed from what it describes as the EU’s “failed” migration policy and EUR 2 billion more allocated to border protection. The group is specifically demanding reimbursement for Hungary’s border-protection costs.

“We demand that the illegally forced-through migration pact be reviewed and withdrawn,” Fidesz-KDNP said.

The group is also seeking to double the EU’s agricultural crisis fund from EUR 450 million to EUR 900 million, citing the damage caused by drought. It said recent dry conditions had reduced cereal and maize yields by 20–30%, while livestock farmers have also been struggling with damaged pastures and soaring feed prices.

Fidesz also targets Erasmus funding

Fidesz-KDNP has once again proposed placing Erasmus funding for Hungary’s foundation-run universities into reserve until the European Commission releases the money.

The issue has already begun to change, however. Education Minister Judit Lannert announced last week that Erasmus will return to Hungary’s universities from the 2026/2027 academic year, with students at all 21 universities previously affected by restrictions once again able to participate.

If you missed it: Erasmus returns to Hungary – Hungarian university students can once again study abroad!

Fidesz nevertheless accused the Tisza government of failing to resolve the dispute and called for the Commission to immediately lift the restrictions.

The group also proposed cutting EUR 250 million from EU funding programmes supporting what it described as “left-wing” civil society organisations, arguing that member states should not face politically motivated pressure from EU institutions.

World.title: Hungarian Ferencváros fans face police complaint after ‘We’ll beat you to death’ banner
World.content:
Police are examining a complaint over a threatening banner displayed by Ferencváros supporters during Sunday’s derby against Újpest, while the club says it “basically condemns all threats”.

The Ferencváros–Újpest derby ended in a 2-2 draw on Sunday, but the football result was overshadowed by a bitter exchange between the two fanbases in the stands. Among the banners displayed by Ferencváros (Fradi) supporters was a particularly disturbing message directed at anyone who might “hurt” the club:

“Love Fradi and you’ll be happy. If you hurt Fradi, you’ll be dead. Love Fradi and support them with us; if you hurt Fradi, we’ll beat you to death.”

The message has now resulted in a police complaint. According to Magyar Hang, the Budapest Police Headquarters (BRFK) has received a report concerning the banner and is currently examining its contents. A criminal investigation has not yet been formally launched over the threat.

Fradi asked to condemn threats

Telex contacted Ferencváros to ask whether the club condemned the message and how it viewed a separate incident in which a critic of club president Gábor Kubatov was allegedly attacked by masked men after a men’s handball match.

The club initially declined to comment on the attack, saying that a police investigation was under way and that it would not discuss the case until that process was completed. After repeated questions, however, Ferencváros gave a brief response concerning the threatening banner:

“The FTC basically condemns all threats.”

The club’s press office repeatedly shifted attention to a banner displayed by Újpest supporters reading “Gábor Kubatov, start worrying”, asking whether the media intended to comment on what it considered a threat against its president.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

The controversy surrounding Fradiváros

The increasingly hostile atmosphere is linked partly to the long-running Fradiváros controversy, which concerns billions of forints in state funding awarded to Ferencváros for the development of its Népliget sports complex.

Ferencváros received almost HUF 25 billion (about EUR 63 million) in state support in 2016 and 2017 for the project. However, little of the planned development materialised. According to the club’s accounts, much of the money was reported as operating and material expenditure, while HUF 11.2 billion was spent on signing professional footballers.

The Hungarian Interior Ministry has filed a criminal complaint over the matter, and an investigation is under way. Journalists investigating the spending have subsequently become targets of threats from sections of the club’s fanbase. A banner recently appeared referring to journalist János Kele, who reported extensively on the Fradiváros case, while another message targeted journalist András Murányi.

If you missed it: Ferencváros narrowly beaten by Real Madrid at packed Groupama Arena

From threats to an alleged attack

The controversy has also moved beyond banners and online messages. Last week, four masked individuals allegedly attacked Zoltán Lajos Németh, who runs the C-Közép supporters’ blog and has long been critical of Kubatov. He was reportedly sprayed with pepper spray and called a “traitorous lackey” following the Ferencváros–Dabas handball match.

Featured image is illustration. Photo: Facebook/Ferencvárosi Torna Club

World.title: Kosovo Parliament to Reconvene, ‘Chaos’ Looms over Election of President
World.content:
Kosovo’s new parliament reconvenes for its inaugural session on Wednesday, despite continued uncertainty over whether lawmakers will agree on the election of a head-of-state.

The session started on August 6, following elections in June, but was paused after the victorious Vetevendosje party asked for “more time” for negotiations with other parties on the candidate for Kosovo’s next president.

At the end of the month, Vetevendosje leader Albin Kurti and his counterpart from the opposition Democratic League of Kosovo, LDK, Lumir Abdixhiku announced that their parties would both back Judge Bekim Sejdiu as president, only for a third of the LDK’s MPs to cry foul.

Such is the depth of animosity between Vetevendosje and its rivals, constituting parliament and electing a president has become a major challenge, complicated by a rift within the LDK over Abdixhiku’s leadership.

World.title: Albanian Port Bars Alleged Russian-Linked ‘Shadow Fleet’ Oil Tanker
World.content:
The Harbour Master’s Office in the Albanian port of Durres has barred the oil tanker Hanuman from entering the port after Ukraine’s military intelligence identified the vessel as part of Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet”, which Moscow uses to transport oil and petroleum products and evade sanctions.

The Intelligence Directorate at Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence, known as the GUR, welcomed Albania’s move as an example of international cooperation in enforcing sanctions and restricting maritime routes used by Moscow to export oil.

“Albania’s decision not to allow the ‘Hanuman’ to enter its port is an important demonstration of international solidarity in enforcing sanctions,” the GUR said.

“Joint actions by Ukraine and its foreign partners are steadily limiting the Kremlin’s ability to use maritime trade routes to circumvent sanctions, forcing the aggressor state to take responsibility for its actions,” it added.

The Hanuman was flying under the flag of Sierra Leone when it was barred from entering Durres port on August 29.

Data published by the GUR shows that since the start of 2025, the Hanuman has transported at least 452,000 tonnes of fuel out of Russia.

Most of its voyages originated from Novorossiysk, one of Russia’s main Black Sea ports, with destinations including Turkey, Senegal, the United Arab Emirates and a ship-to-ship transfer area near the Italian city of Augusta.

The GUR claims a Russian company, Altoprae Marine, based in Novorossiysk, provided logistical support for these voyages, which it links to a manager from the circle of sanctioned Russian oligarch Gennady Timchenko, a longtime ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The GUR also links Altoprae Marine to the operations of vessels owned by Rosewood Shipping, which Ukrainian authorities claim is controlled by Oksana Marchenko, the wife of pro-Russian Ukrainian politician Viktor Medvedchuk, a longtime ally of Putin.

Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet” consists of a network of tankers it uses to keep its oil exports moving after Western sanctions were imposed over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

These vessels often operate under the flags of third countries and through ownership structures that are difficult to trace.

The G7 countries and the European Union introduced a price cap on Russian seaborne oil in late 2022, along with restrictions on insurance, financing and other services related to its transport.

Albania, an EU candidate country and NATO member, has aligned itself with the EU’s sanctions against Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Maritime traffic data show that the Hanuman previously visited the Port of Durres in November 2025.

A BIRN investigation published in May 2026 identified the tanker as part of a list of vessels suspected of transporting Russian oil or grain stolen from Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia.

The vessels on the list had visited Albanian ports since 2022, raising questions about the enforcement of sanctions imposed by Albania against Moscow.

World.title: Romanians Flock to Venerate Saint Anne’s Relics in Bucharest
World.content:
“We are particularly happy to welcome the bringing of the relics of St Anne, the grandmother of our Lord Jesus Christ and the mother of the Most Holy Mother of God,” Patriarch Daniel, head of the Romanian Orthodox Church, said after receiving the relics at his patriarchal residence. He described the opportunity to venerate them as “a great blessing”.

In the Orthodox calendar, St Anne is celebrated on September 9. She is traditionally regarded as a protector of families, children and motherhood. The relics will remain at the Bucharest church until September 10, with the church open daily from 7 a.m. until 10 p.m., or longer if pilgrims are still waiting to enter.

World.title: EU Leaders Condemn ‘Shocking’ Glorification of Mladic at Belgrade Funeral
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Senior European Union figures have condemned the military honours and glorification of the convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic at his funeral in Belgrade, warning that the scenes undermined Serbia’s European aspirations.

In a joint statement European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa described images from Monday’s funeral as “shocking”, stressing that Mladic died while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

“The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable,” Von der Leyen and Costa wrote on X on Tuesday. “They demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe’s recent history and contradict the values underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union.”

Several Serbian ministers, including Defence Minister Bratislav Gasic and Justice Minister Nenad Vujic, attended the funeral of Mladic, the former commander of the Bosnian Serb Army, who was buried with military honours in Belgrade.

Officials from Bosnia’s Serb-dominated Republika Srpska entity also attended, as well as an estimated 16,000 mourners, according to the Archive of Public Gatherings, which gauges attendance sizes at large gatherings.

Until his death on August 27 at the UN Detention Unit in the Netherlands, Mladic was serving a life sentence after being convicted of genocide and other wartime crimes.

The EU criticism comes at a politically sensitive moment in Serbia, a candidate for membership of the bloc, where elections are approaching and relations between Brussels and Belgrade have already faced strains over democratic standards.

A group of 118 Serbian professors and researchers wrote on Tuesday in a letter to Von der Leyen ahead of her possible visit to Serbia in October, warning that a meeting with President Aleksandar Vucic during an election campaign could be portrayed by pro-government media as European support for the incumbent authorities.

“We are not asking you to support the student movement, the opposition, or any electoral list. We are asking you to support no one,” the academics said, urging Von der Leyen to consider postponing the visit until after the elections if it could not be protected from political manipulation.

Condemnation also came from US politicians. House of Representatives members Greg Murphy and Marc Veasey said on Monday that Mladic’s funeral was “not an occasion for his glorification”, warning that genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals deepen ethnic divisions and undermine Bosnia and Herzegovina’s stability.

The two US politicians also called for targeted sanctions against individuals who threaten Bosnia’s peace and stability or undermine the 1995 Dayton peace deal framework.

Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Oncu Keceli meanwhile said it was “unacceptable” for the funeral to be exploited in a way that amounted to denying grave crimes and human suffering.

Ankara said rejecting international court judgments or portraying convicted perpetrators as heroes deepens the suffering of victims and their relatives and damages peace and reconciliation in the Balkans.

Turkey said the region needed to learn lessons from the past and build a “peaceful, prosperous and shared future”, while commemorating the victims of the Srebrenica genocide and all innocent people killed during the Bosnian war.

Condemnation has continued to come from neighbouring states as well, with Montenegro’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressing concern for Mladic’s victims.

“It is our obligation to preserve the dignity and memory of the victims, to preserve the truth about crimes and individual responsibility for them, and to resolutely oppose any attempt to deny genocide, war crimes and other serious violations of international humanitarian law,” the Montenegrin ministry said in a written statement on Tuesday.

On Monday, Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Foreign Minister Elmedin Konakovic warned that the Serbian leadership is risking “complete isolation in the region”, while Croatia’s Foreign Minister Gordan Grlic Radman said that “glorifying this war criminal is truly incompatible with European values”.

World.title: Falling Profits Cloud Horizons for Turkey’s Booming Tourist Industry
World.content:
Turkey continues to draw millions of holidaymakers to its beaches, resorts and historic sites, but beneath the headline visitor numbers, the country’s tourism industry is showing signs of strain.

After a record year, Turkey entered 2026 with high hopes, having hosted nearly 64 million visitors and generated 65.23 billion US dollars in tourism revenue in 2025, up 2.7 and 6.8 per cent respectively compared to 2024, and ranking fourth globally for international tourist arrivals.

However, official figures show that visitor numbers actually fell 5.1 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while tourism revenue dropped 2.6 per cent to 15.87 billion US dollars.

Meanwhile, industry data cited by Turizm News showed average hotel occupancy falling from 40.17 per cent in the first half of 2025 to 36.80 per cent in the same period this year.

World.title: BIRN Fact-Check: Has Romania Made a Success of Post-Pandemic EU Funding?
World.content:
In the final two weeks of August, Romania was suddenly awash with positive news. Almost every day brought reports of a renovated hospital or school, new stretches of motorways or railway lines, completed water and sewage networks, or newly rehabilitated public buildings.

Authorities announced new green hydrogen production facilities, reforestation projects covering large areas of land and other investments, all presented as evidence of Romania’s rapid modernisation.

The wave of announcements was driven mainly by the August 31 deadline for it to complete numerous projects financed through the European Union’s post-pandemic recovery programme, the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, PNRR.

Authorities rushed to showcase projects launched, completed, or brought close to completion, often presenting them as tangible proof that Romania had successfully used the unprecedented EU funding made available after the pandemic.

World.title: Czech PM’s Balkan Schengen Illusion Is a Security Risk for Europe
World.content:
A geopolitical trap

In the case of the Western Balkan states, the issue of Schengen accession carries a strong geopolitical dimension. While even the harshest EU sceptics did not question Croatia or Romania’s pro-Western orientation, fundamental questions remain about the true foreign policy orientation of some Western Balkan states and their willingness to align their policies with Europe.

This issue is particularly evident in Serbia, which has maintained close ties with Russia and China as part of a foreign policy that seeks to balance competing geopolitical interests, while remaining reluctant to bring its policies fully into line with those of Europe.

Certain recent gestures by President Vucic, such as hosting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky or rearming the country’s air force by replacing Russian MiGs with French Rafale fighters, do not signal a Serbian turn away from Russia, but are merely a reflection of his long-standing policy of geopolitical balancing, which is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain as geopolitical tensions between Europe and Russia escalate.

A key problem with Babis’s proposed accelerated Schengen accession is Serbian visa policy, which precisely reflects the country’s geopolitical balancing act. Serbia is one of the last European states to maintain a visa-free regime with Russia, despite EU pressure to terminate it and align its visa policy with that of the EU.

In Serbia’s case, this is no minor unfulfilled task. Beyond its considerable symbolic significance, the open-door policy for Russians carries a strong economic and security dimension. Over the last four years of Russia’s war against Ukraine, Belgrade has become a major hub for Russians traveling to Europe for various reasons. Serbian state airlines operate regular direct flights to five destinations in the European part of Russia. Belgrade Airport is the only one on the European continent offering such connections, making it a key transit hub on this route.

A significant number of Russians have also settled permanently or temporarily in Serbia, which is not only easily accessible to them but also culturally relatively close. While the Serbian border police registered nearly a million single entries by Russians between 2022 and 2024, estimates put the number of Russians residing in Serbia long term at around 100,000. The Serbian government has accommodated this trend with generous residence permits and citizenship grants, in some cases through accelerated procedures “in the state interest” or even to Russians under sanctions.

What statistics fail to capture is the political profile of this new Russian diaspora. It is presumed to be a mix of pragmatically minded Russians, many of whom are successfully building businesses in Serbia; anti-Putin exiles; and prominent figures directly linked to Putin. The proportion of these individual groups remains unknown, and judging by recorded intelligence activities targeting the Russian opposition in Belgrade, Moscow is seeking that answer as well.

Furthermore, Serbia is not merely a venue for Russian intelligence services to monitor their own opposition, but also a safe staging ground for operations elsewhere in Europe. For instance, BIRN recently documented the Russian recruitment of volunteers in Serbia for the war against Ukraine, as well as training centres for hybrid operations in Moldova. As-yet unconfirmed reports of a Serbian citizen’s involvement in a hybrid attack in Leipzig and the use of Serbia for the transit of Russian operatives provide further evidence of Serbia’s role in Russian activities on European soil.

It is precisely Russia’s ongoing intelligence links with Serbia that expose the main flaw in Babis’s statements on Serbia’s rapid Schengen accession. While the prime minister defends such a plan as a means of combating illegal migration, he completely overlooks another risk that cannot be ignored during a period of escalating Russian operations against Europe. Czechia’s European allies are well aware of this risk and for this reason won’t permit any hasty expansion of the Schengen Area.

Serbia may have its place in the EU and Schengen someday, provided it genuinely desires membership and meets at least the basic political and security conditions. Ending its visa-free policy with Russia certainly ranks among them, regardless of the Czech prime minister’s disregard for the issue.

Petr Čermák is a Research Fellow at the Association for International Affairs focusing on Western Balkan politics.

The opinions expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of BIRN.

World.title: Ratko Mladic Buried with Military Honours in Serbia, Thousands Attend Funeral
World.content:
Large crowds of mourners, including Serbian ministers, gathered in Belgrade on Monday for the funeral of Ratko Mladic, who died in detention while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Troops lined the road and police saluted the coffin, which was draped with the flags of Serbia and Republika Srpska, as it was transported to Topcider Cemetery from the Church of St. Luke, where the head of the Serbian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Porfirije, led a funeral service.

The Patriarch declared that Mladic’s name will “remain deeply woven into the memory and prayers of the vast majority of our Serbian Orthodox people, who feel and cultivate deep gratitude toward him”.

A Serbian Army honour guard gave a three-volley salute as Mladic’s coffin was lowered into the grave, and mourners shouted “Long live Ratko Mladic” and “Glory to the hero”. He was buried next to his daughter Ana, who committed suicide in 1994.

Serbian Defence Minister Bratislav Gasic, Minister without Portfolio Nenad Popovic and Minister for Labour, Employment, Veterans and Social Affairs Milica Djurdjevic Stamenkovski attended the funeral, as did war veterans in military uniforms.

From Republika Srpska came Milorad Dodik, the head of the ruling coalition in the Serb-dominated entity, and Zeljka Cvijanovic, the Serb member of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s tripartite presidency. The Russian ambassador to Serbia Aleksandar Bocan-Harchenko came to pay condolences to the Mladic family.

But European Union officials, the foreign ministers of neighbouring Croatia and Bosnia, and survivors of wartime crimes committed by Mladic’s forces strongly criticised the commemoration of the genocide convict.

The EU warned that the glorification of war criminals and genocide denial “contradict the most fundamental European values and have no place in the EU or in EU candidate countries”.

T-shirts celebrate Mladic’s wartime actions

From early on Monday, hundreds of mourners streamed towards the Church of St. Luke, some walking several kilometres to pay tribute to the war criminal they consider a Serbian hero, despite his convictions by the Hague Tribunal.

Many carried flags and wore T-shirts depicting Mladic or symbols of Republika Srpska and its army, which he led during the war. One T-shirt slogan read: “Ratko Mladic – Is it a crime to defend the Serbian people?”

“Now even the [football] supporters are together, now we’re all together,” said one man, referring to the fact that both fans of Red Star and Partizan, Belgrade’s main football clubs, had paid tribute to Ratko Mladic during their weekend derby.

A younger Mladic supporter standing next to him was in tears. “He tried to protect us, and now we are here to see him off,” he said.

At noon, the Patriarch Porfirije led the funeral service, saying that Mladic “stood at the head of the army of his people and carried a great responsibility and burden, made a sacrifice, and laid down his life for the freedom, defence and survival of his people”.

Following the service, members of the Serbian Armed Forces carried the coffin from the church to the funeral procession heading towards Topcider Cemetery.

In the procession, Mladic’s son Darko carried a sabre, while other family members carried Mladic’s military decorations and a photograph of him. Mladic’s wife, Bosiljka, walked behind the coffin.

Along the route between the church and the cemetery, water tankers and temporary public toilets had been installed for those attending. The city of Belgrade deployed significant resources, providing the water supplies, electric transport vehicles and city-run security services.

Free transport was offered from Bosnia and most towns in Serbia for anyone who wanted to pay their respects, Reuters news agency and media outlets in Serbia and Montenegro reported. Dozens of buses travelled from Republika Srpska, while organised bus transport was also arranged from Montenegro.

At the ceremony, flags bearing the deceased general’s image were flown and a sound system had been set up so mourners could hear Mladic’s son Darko speak.

Darko Mladic thanked the mourners for what he called a “magnificent farewell.”

“Thank you, my brothers, for coming to decide whether my father is a hero or a criminal,” he said.

Mladic was then buried with a ceremonial volley, an honour traditionally reserved for senior military officials. Mladic held the rank of general in the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA, during the early 1990s but legal experts in Serbia are divided on whether there is any basis for a funeral with state or army honours, given that he was convicted of genocide

Anger in Bosnia and Croatia

Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Foreign Minister Elmedin Konakovic condemned Monday’s commemoration of Mladic, accusing Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic of “leading Serbia towards complete isolation in the region”.

“We saw a war criminal being given the highest military honours. We saw a large number of Serbian government officials attending the funeral and commemoration,” Konakovic told reporters.

Konakovic said Vucic had been “cowardly” to stay away from the funeral, but claimed that “we all know very well that he is the organiser, implementer and personally the most responsible person”. Vucic avoided the issue of attendance at the funeral by saying he was busy on Monday meeting Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

Konakovic said draft letters had been prepared for the US, EU and UK, adding that Bosnia will ask the EU “whether it truly respects its own principles”. He added that he will seek to reduce contact with Serbia and withdraw personnel from Bosnia’s embassy in Belgrade. “There will be no more talks on economic cooperation with Serbia while I am here,” he added.

Croatia’s Foreign Minister Gordan Grlic Radman also slammed Monday’s commemorations in Belgrade – and warned that they could affect Serbia’s EU accession process.

“Glorifying this war criminal is truly incompatible with European values,” Grlic Radman declared.

He noted the glorification of Mladic not only in Serbia, but also in Montenegro. “This is above all an insult to the victims, survivors and their families,” he said.

He called for action to be taken over threats to European values in countries that are candidates for EU membership, which include Serbia and Montenegro.

Mladic was found guilty of some of the worst atrocities in Europe since World War II by the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia in The Hague.

He was convicted of genocide of Bosniaks in Srebrenica in 1995, the persecution and extermination of Bosniaks and Croats across the country, terrorising the population of Sarajevo with a campaign of shelling and sniper attacks, and taking UN peacekeepers hostage.

World.title: Former Croatian PM Seeks Suspension of Serbian EU Accession Talks
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – Former Croatian PM Jadranka Kosor is seeking total suspension of all Serbian EU accession talks, calling on Ursula von der Leyen to take action.

Former Croatian Prime Minister Jadranka Kosor has called on the European Commission to completely suspend Serbia’s EU accession negotiations following today’s mass farewell for Ratko Mladić in Belgrade, which was held with the highest state and military honours. “After today’s funeral, involving the anti-civilisational bowing of Serbia to a war criminal convicted of genocide, I expect the incompetent European Commission and its incompetent leader Ursula von der Leyen to fully suspend Serbia’s accession negotiations for entry into the EU. That is the minimum,” Kosor wrote on X.

a serbian state funeral for a genocidal maniac

Index reports that thousands of people gathered in Belgrade to bid a final farewell to the former commander of the Army of Republika Srpska. Disgraced Ratko Mladić was buried at Topčider Cemetery with state honours, in the presence of members of the Serbian Army and an honour guard. Numerous Serbian officials, the political leadership of Republika Srpska, and the Russian ambassador to Serbia attended the funeral. Before the burial, his coffin was displayed in the Church of St. Luke, where the service was led by Patriarch Porfirije. On the coffin were his officer’s cap and sabre, and members of the army and veterans of the former Army of Republika Srpska stood beside it. The Serbian Government had previously sent a state aircraft to collect Mladić’s remains from The Hague, and soldiers carried his coffin, covered with the Serbian flag, out of the plane. A commemoration was also held for him on Saturday in an official facility of the Serbian Army.

serbia honours one of the worst monsters of the 20th century

Mladić died on the 27th of August at the age of 84 in The Hague, where he was serving a life sentence. He had suffered several quite serious strokes and his health had been declining rapidly for some time. He was finally convicted of committing genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity, and war crimes during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. His forces were responsible, among other things, for the massacre of more than 8,000 innocent Bosniak men and boys in Srebrenica in July 1995, as well as for the multi-year, dreadful siege of Sarajevo.

the eu’s position is clear – no glorification of war crimes and war criminals

The European Union has already very clearly warned Serbia over the glorification of the vile Ratko Mladić. European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos cancelled a planned visit to Serbia after a state aircraft brought his body to Belgrade. The European External Action Service stated that the glorification of war criminals, denial of genocide, and revisionism have no place either in the European Union or in candidate countries. Serbia has otherwise held candidate status for EU membership and has been conducting accession negotiations since 2014.

World.title: Osijek Company to Develop Unmanned Systems & More in Vukovar
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – An Osijek company is set to develop unmanned systems in Vukovar and more as part of a five million euro project.

A new production facility is being built in the Vukovar Business Zone by the Osijek-based company GAUSS d.o.o., which focuses on the development of digital and high-tech solutions. Poslovni reports that last week, representatives of the investors, together with Deputy Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Ivan Penava, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries David Vlajčić, and State Secretary Dario Tišov, toured the investment worth slightly less than five million euros.

The new facility is expected to start operating during the second quarter of next year. It will develop and produce unmanned systems using artificial intelligence, smart software and other advanced tech. Hrvoje Sagrak, Director of Business Development and Sales at the Osijek company, emphasised that coming to Vukovar is an opportunity to transfer the experience gained through cooperation with international partners, especially in the United Arab Emirates.

“It is truly a great honour for us to be here in Vukovar because we have a unique opportunity to transfer the business experience and know-how that we have acquired through cooperation with partners abroad, primarily in the United Arab Emirates, to Croatia. Right here we want to build a point that will be a centre of excellence and a centre of knowledge about high technologies,” said Sagrak.

ai, unmanned systems and more

The future facility will not deal only with the production of aircraft. It will develop systems that include smart software, artificial intelligence and other devices, and the applications could range from surveillance and protection to fire prevention, protection of critical infrastructure and border monitoring. Special emphasis will be placed on the rapid development of new products and turning ideas into prototypes. Industry 4.0 technologies and 3D printers will be used so that new solutions can be designed, tested and verified more quickly and cheaply.

In the initial phase, around ten experts with multidisciplinary knowledge in electrical engineering and other modern fields are expected to work at the facility. “It isn’t about the number of employees itself, but about what will be developed through such a venture and spread throughout the entire ecosystem,” Sagrak said, adding that the facility has the possibility of further expansion.

the future has (finally) arrived in vukovar, a town scarred by the past

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister David Vlajčić recalled that the story of this investment has been ongoing since the time when he was assistant director of the Vukovar Business Zone. “The investor then took a plot and began developing something that combines hardware and software, i.e. solutions that we do not have in Croatia today. Such investments require a trained workforce, but at the same time they open up the potential for smart technologies from all over the world to come right here, to Croatia and Vukovar, and for us to have something special on the territory of the European Union,” said Vlajčić.

The importance of the investment was also highlighted by Deputy Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Ivan Penava, who believes that the project places Vukovar alongside modern technological environments. “The future has arrived in Vukovar,” Penava said, emphasising that artificial intelligence, 3D printers and unmanned aerial vehicles represent high-tech industry, and by connecting them integrated production is created.

“When we talk about artificial intelligence, 3D printers or unmanned aerial vehicles, each of these technologies on its own already represents high-tech industry. However, here we’re talking about integrated production and connecting all of that through one product. All of this has today, on a symbolic level, arrived in Vukovar,” said Penava. He added that talks with the investors lasted about two years and emphasised that their arrival is important because, despite economic logic, they are choosing Croatia and Vukovar also because of their connection with this area.

The investment worth slightly less than five million euros represents a new step in the development of the Vukovar Business Zone, as well as in the effort to position Vukovar as a place for the development and production of advanced technological solutions for the domestic and global market.

World.title: 3% More Vehicles on Croatian Motorways Than This Time in 2025
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – There have been 3% more vehicles recorded on Croatian motorways this year than back during this period in 2025.

From the beginning of the year until the end of August, 56.5 million cars passed along Croatian motorways, which is an increase of 1.6 million, or three percent, compared with the same period last year, HRT reports. “Croatia as a tourist country is recognised not only for its natural beauty, but above all for the safety it offers to all tourists, and this increase in traffic is a result of that,” said Ivan Ribičić, Director of the Toll Collection Sector.

Poslovni reports that the busiest periods, according to Ribičić, are the end of July and the beginning of August. “All three summer months were very successful. Compared with last year, that is 300,000 more vehicles. These are excellent results, he said. In the last three to four years, large traffic jams on Mondays have become increasingly frequent. This weekend also exceeded expectations. On Sunday by 18:00, 100,000 vehicles were recorded at the Lučko entrance alone, which is more than last year.

In the autumn, works on the Zagreb bypass are finally due to begin, which should make passage between Zagreb East and Zagreb West easier, as well as access to the Lučko toll booth.

World.title: New Poll Lays Bare Worst Result for HDZ in the Last Two Years
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – A brand new poll has showcased the absolute worst result for HDZ in the last two years, with Prime Minister Andrej Plenković personally scoring very poorly.

Public dissatisfaction over the hazardous waste affair in Lika has been reflected on the political scene, as shown by the latest monthly CRO Demoskop survey. Index reports that according to the poll conducted for RTL this month, both HDZ and SDP recorded a significant drop in support, with the ruling party, being HDZ, falling to its lowest level in the past two years.

If parliamentary elections had been held at the beginning of the month, HDZ would still have been the relative winner. Index reports that the CRO Demoskop survey was conducted by the agency Promocija plus from 1 to 3 September using a telephone survey (CATI) on a representative sample of 1,000 respondents. The sample was stratified by counties and settlement size, with control of socio-demographic characteristics. The standard sampling error is ±3.04% at a 95% confidence level.

most and Možemo! outperform hdz and sdp

According to the latest poll, HDZ has the support of 25.3% of voters, a drop from 27% seen in July. This is also the party’s weakest result since April 2024. SDP is in second place with 20.5% support, also recording a decline from 21.5% in July and its lowest rating in the current term. Možemo! ranked third with 12.9% support, a slight increase from 12.2% in July. The biggest rise was recorded by Most, which jumped from 7.7% to 9.5%. It is followed by the party Drito with 1.8% and Domovinski pokret with 1.6%. Both parties have slightly lower support than in July. Most thus recorded a rise of 1.8 percentage points, and Možemo! of 0.7. HDZ is down by 1.7 percentage points, SDP by 1.0, and Drito and DP by 0.5 percentage points each.

Other parties have support below 1.5%. Above one percent are Domino (1.4%), Centar (1.1%), Pravo i pravda (1.1%), IDS (1.0%) and Nezavisna platforma Sjever (1.0%). Below that threshold are HNS (0.9%), Hrvatski suverenisti (0.8%), HSU (0.8%), HSS (0.7%), HSLS (0.4%) and Fokus (0.3%). All other parties together have two percent support, while undecided voters stand at 16.9%.

president milanović receives the most positive rating among politicians, while pm plenković receives the worst

The most positively perceived politicians are as follows:

Zoran Milanović – 23%

Andrej Plenković – 15.6%

Tomislav Tomašević – 4.1%

Marin Miletić – 3.8%

Ivana Kekin – 2.9%

Dalija Orešković – 2.7%

Nikola Grmoja – 2.5%

Ivan Anušić – 2.2%

Sandra Benčić – 1.6%

Biljana Borzan – 1.5%

The most negatively perceived politicians are as follows:

Andrej Plenković – 37.3%

Zoran Milanović – 12.3%

Tomislav Tomašević – 5.6%

Sandra Benčić – 2.5%

Ivan Penava – 2.3%

Milorad Pupovac – 2.1%

Dalija Orešković – 1.8%

Hrvoje Zekanović – 1.6%

Siniša Hajdaš Dončić – 1.4%

Andrija Mikulić – 1.4%

most believe the country is heading in the wrong direction

This September, only 17.5% of citizens believe that Croatia is moving in a good direction, a drop from 20.2% in July. At the same time, the share of those who think the direction is wrong rose from 70% to 74.6%. Undecided stand at 7.9%. Among HDZ voters optimism prevails and 55.4% of them consider the direction good. Voters of opposition parties are considerably more critical.

President Zoran Milanović received an average grade of 3.08 for his work. He received the highest grade from SDP voters (3.97) and the lowest from HDZ voters (2.32). The work of the Croatian Parliament was rated 2.16. It received the highest grade from HDZ voters (3.0) and the lowest from Možemo! platform voters (1.69). The Government received a grade of 2.23 for its work, the lowest grade in the past year. HDZ voters rated the Government’s work at 3.81, while voters of other parties were considerably stricter. Support for the Government’s policy fell to 25.7%, compared with 27.6% in July.

the appalling lika hazardous waste affair is the hot topic

The hazardous waste affair in Lika and other parts of the country was the most important topic of the past month for as many as 40.4% of respondents. This is one of the highest results for a single event since measurements began in 2004. In second place in importance is the fire in Omiš and the surrounding area, which 27.9% of citizens singled out as a key event. These are followed by the heatwave (5.4%), inflation (3.5%), the extraordinary session of Parliament (3.0%) and the rise in fuel prices (2.9%). Among the more important topics are also sporting successes, Thompson’s concert in Vukovar and arrests related to arson.

World.title: Slaven Bilić Surprises with New Names in Croatia’s Nations League Squad
World.content:
Croatia head coach Slaven Bilić announced the squad list he’s counting on for the upcoming Nations League fixtures in September and October.

Croatia have four competitive matches in the space of 11 days ahead of them, and head coach Bilić will be relying on the following players for this “campaign”:

“Summer has passed, that period where I did a lot of thinking, a lot of talking. The time to gather has come, and I think we’re ready now. I talked a lot with the players, watched, thought it over, and arrived at the final list. This is a specific situation — it’s the first time we’ve had four Nations League matches in around ten days. I don’t want this to disrupt my work. We’ve gone with 23 + 3.”

Player list

GOALKEEPERS: Dominik Livaković (Barcelona), Dominik Kotarski (Dinamo), Ivor Pandur (Rangers)

DEFENDERS: Joško Gvardiol (Manchester City), Josip Juranović (Union Berlin), Josip Šutalo (Lazio), Luka Vušković (Brighton), Ivan Smolčić (Como), Josip Stanišić (Bayern), Martin Erlić (Midtjylland)

MIDFIELDERS: Luka Modrić (Milan), Mateo Kovačić (Manchester City), Mario Pašalić (Atalanta), Nikola Vlašić (Torino), Petar Sučić (Inter), Luka Sučić (Real Sociedad), Josip Mišić (Dinamo), Martin Baturina (Como)

FORWARDS: Ivan Perišić (PSV), Andrej Kramarić (Hoffenheim), Ante Budimir (Osasuna), Igor Matanović (Freiburg), Franjo Ivanović (Lens), Dion Drena Beljo (Dinamo), Marco Pašalić (Orlando City), Petar Musa (Dallas FC)

ON STANDBY: Karlo Letica (Luzern), Marin Pongračić (Fiorentina), Kristijan Jakić (Augsburg), Nikola Moro (Bologna), Lovro Majer (AEK), Toni Fruk (Rijeka)

Bilić’s debut on September 26th

The big news of the weekend just gone is that Luka Modrić has confirmed he will continue playing for Croatia.

Luka Modrić has made 202 appearances for Croatia to date, and will now work with Slaven Bilić again after 14 years.

The squad list also features some new names, while some players will lose the place they held in the national team’s previous campaigns.

As for the Nations League schedule, what lies ahead for Croatia is anything but easy.

Bilić’s side travel to Czechia on September 26th, then to Spain three days later.

Two home matches follow: against England on October 3rd and Spain on October 6th.

Croatia’s fixture schedule in Nations League Group A3:

26 September, 20:45: Czechia – Croatia

29 September, 20:45: Spain – Croatia

3 October, 18:00: Croatia – England (Rujevica Stadium, Rijeka)

6 October, 20:45: Croatia – Spain (Poljud Stadium, Split)

World.title: Nikola Šubić Zrinski – The Croat Who Stopped 100,000 Ottomans
World.content:
September the 7th, 2026 – Turning the clock all the way back to the 7th of September 1566, and we meet the famed Nikola Šubić Zrinski, the Croat who stopped 100,000 Ottomans, but lost his life during the final charge.

Nikola Šubić Zrinski was a Croatian nobleman, ban (viceroy) and soldier who lived during the 16th century and is remembered as a defender of Christianity throughout Europe. Index writes that he is best known for the Battle of Szigetvár, in which the sultan himself also lost his life. In Croatia, he holds additional importance because he elevated the Zrinski noble family to the status of the most powerful Croatian family of all.

he never shied away from battling the fearsome ottoman forces

He was born sometime during 1508. We don’t know exactly where he entered the world, but we know he had five brothers and sisters. His father was Nikola Šubić and his mother Jelena Karlović. Nikola’s political activity did not come only from the fact that he was a nobleman; the Karlović family had a long tradition of state functions. Nikola’s uncle Ivan Karlović later served as ban. The brave Zrinski was primarily a soldier. After finishing military school, Šubić joined the ongoing war and defended Vienna in 1529, at which time he was noticed by many nobles and military officials. After the siege he was rewarded with a golden chain and received a horse.

The conflict with the Ottomans only continued. When he inherited the estate in the Una valley in 1534, he also inherited the obligation to pay tribute to the Ottomans. Nikola truly did not want to pay tribute to the enemy, so he provoked a conflict over the fortress of Dubica in order to justify not paying the taxes.

habsburg or zapolya?

At the same time the Kingdom of Hungary was very unstable. After the death of Vladislav II Jagiellon at Mohács, the whole country split into two camps: one favoured the Habsburgs and wanted to bring them to power in Hungary and Croatia, while the other favoured the local Hungarian nobleman John Zápolya. Nikola Šubić Zrinski considered Ferdinand Habsburg the better and wiser choice, and he had already become acquainted with the Habsburgs during the siege of Vienna. That is why, on his own initiative, he decided to kill the nobleman Johann Katzianer, who had rejected the Habsburgs and sworn loyalty to Zápolya. He captured Katzianer’s fortress of Kostajnica, but soon handed it over to the Ottomans, from whom he expected retaliation for refusing to pay tribute.

the zrinskis head north…

From the 1540s on, he was given administration of the whole of Međimurje. He soon moved there, renovated the castle in Čakovec, and after a few years received the right to collect taxes himself and to settle serfs in the area. At the same time he became Ban of Croatia, a title he held until 1556. He left the “office” of ban because he was dissatisfied that he had failed to raise more funds for the fight against the Ottomans. He wanted someone more capable to take the position while he continued to wage war against the enemy. He immediately received the position of treasurer in Hungary (Hungarian nobles were inclined to give him whatever he wanted because he was highly respected even before Szigetvár) and fought the Ottomans twice. He believed he already knew their strategies well and rushed into war with them whenever possible.

the famous battle of Szigetvár

The next opportunity presented itself in 1566 when he was staying in the fortress of Szigetvár. Szigetvár is located in Hungary on the shortest route to Vienna. Suleiman the Magnificent led 100,000 men to capture Szigetvár and begin a new siege of Vienna. To them Szigetvár was just another miserable Christian fortress; the Ottomans conquered such places every other day. However, Suleiman the Magnificent was not prepared for what was about to happen. Around 2,000 men, mostly ethnic Croats, decided that the Ottomans would not pass here. As soon as Ottoman infantry approached the gates of Szigetvár, the defenders threw everything they could at them and the enemy withdrew. Szigetvár was constantly bombarded with cannonballs for a full month, and one did not walk in the inner courtyard because of the arrows that fell into the fortress without stopping.

The defenders ate all the food they had, then began to eat their own horses. They maintained their morale largely thanks to Nikola Šubić, who in his classic style still saw only victory. Then came 7 September 1566, and it was clear that that morning the Ottomans would break into the town. Nikola put on a hat and noble attire, left his knight’s armour aside, took his father’s sabre and bravely led his men into the final episode of that nightmare. All the defenders died that morning, and the Ottomans achieved their goal.

an extremely costly goal

But the goal was achieved at too great a cost. The Ottoman army should not have lost a fifth of its force on some stupid and unimportant fortress, nor should it have been delayed there for half the summer. To make matters worse, during the siege Suleiman the Magnificent died, so the army’s morale was weak and worthless. The army was soon recalled and headed home. Nothing came of a new siege of Vienna. The heroic defence of Szigetvár was the main topic of conversation throughout Europe in the following months. Everyone spoke about Nikola Šubić: from Roman and Spanish diplomats who claimed that God had sent him to save Vienna from the Muslims, to the French Cardinal Richelieu who called him “the saviour of Europe and the Christian world.”

His descendants continued to act politically and hold various positions in the new state, the Habsburg Monarchy. Nikola elevated the Zrinskis from an ordinary noble family to the most important family in Croatia. Their influence would mark the following period, right up to the Zrinski-Frankopan conspiracy of 1671.

Nikola Šubić Zrinski remains incredibly relevant to this very day. Legends of his defence of Szigetvár were retold to children in the following centuries, and when the awakening of nationalism began in the 19th century, Nikola became even more popular. Then the 1880 earthquake struck Zagreb and the city had to be rebuilt. About a hundred metres southeast of Zagreb’s main square, construction began on the most beautiful park in the city centre. The park would be named Zrinjevac, or Nikola Šubić Zrinski Square, further immortalising him.
