Tech.title: Should You Buy a New iPhone From Apple, a Carrier or Unlocked? Here’s What to Know
Tech.content:
You might be planning to get a new iPhone, be it the rumored iPhone 18 Pro or the highly anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra. But besides choosing which phone to get, the next big question you might be pondering is “Where should I buy my phone?” Should you get it directly from Apple or through a carrier?

Both methods have their pros and cons, and neither is best for everyone. Perhaps you like the idea of owning your phone outright without going through a third party. Or maybe you’d rather spread out your payments over time. Or perhaps you’re looking to upgrade your phone and switch carriers at the same time. Depending on your answer, you might prefer one path over the other.

In this guide, we walk you through the process of deciding exactly where to buy your new iPhone, be it directly from Apple or through a wireless provider.

Buy directly from Apple

Apple will glady sell you its newest phone and revamped its Upgrade program to let people lease their next iPhone. Jeff Carlson/CNET

Since Apple makes the iPhone, it makes a lot of sense to simply buy the phone directly from the Apple Store. Though buying your iPhone from Apple is a common practice in a lot of countries, it’s not quite as popular here in the US due to the attractive financing options that wireless carriers offer. But buying your phone straight from Apple has its benefits.

The primary reason to go through Apple is that you can buy the phone without being beholden to a wireless carrier. You have options. Instead of locking yourself down to one wireless carrier for multiple years, buying directly from Apple lets you get the phone completely unlocked.



Apple sells both unlocked iPhones and models tied to a specific carrier. The price is nearly the same, depending on which iPhone you get. But Apple drops the price by $30 when you buy and activate a new iPhone on a carrier at the time of purchase for models like the iPhone 17, which costs $829 unlocked or $799 after a carrier discount.

Unlocked models can be used with nearly any carrier you want, whether it’s a major carrier such as T-Mobile and AT&T or a smaller one such as Mint Mobile or Cricket Mobile. You can also swap out carriers every so often if you feel like it. While your iPhone may cost a pretty penny in the initial purchase, you could save on monthly bills in the long run, depending on your plan.

Another strong reason to get an unlocked phone is if you travel a lot and want to use international travel eSIMs from companies such as Airalo or Saily. These eSIMs only work on unlocked phones. Otherwise, you’re stuck with your carrier’s international data plans, which are often a lot more expensive.

If you don’t have the means to purchase the phone outright, you could opt for Apple’s Upgrade program, which lets you lease the phone through Klarna for 12 or 24 months. The phone will still be unlocked, but you’ll have to commit to one of the big three carriers: AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon.

Buy from a wireless provider

T-Mobile, Verizon and AT&T offer a variety of installment plans and trade-in deals on new iPhones. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

While there is a lot of freedom in buying an iPhone directly from Apple, it comes at a considerable cost. Even the most entry-level iPhone will cost you more than $600 upfront, while more premium handsets can easily cost over $1,000. On top of that, rising component costs could mean even higher prices going forward. It’s no wonder that so many Americans opt for carrier-based financing to purchase their phone. The iPhone 18 Pro could see a price hike, according to a Bloomberg report.

Not all carriers will offer financing, but the big three (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon) certainly do. In addition to 12- and 24-month installments, some also offer financing up to 36 months, which is more than what Apple’s Upgrade program does. This can really help spread out your payments if you don’t mind sticking with one carrier for an extended period.

Beyond just being able to pay over time, purchasing an iPhone through your wireless carrier has other benefits, too. Carriers like T-Mobile, for example, offer a 5-year price guarantee on future handsets, which is especially attractive in times of economic uncertainty.

If you do plan to switch carriers when you buy a new phone, there are potentially even more incentives. Carriers often have new phone deals and could even offer financial assistance to pay off your current phone if you make the switch. There are also some that offer steep discounts if you trade in an existing phone. Sometimes, these incentives come in the form of bill credits, instead of an upfront discount or cashback.

Now that you have an idea about buying a new iPhone, check out our comprehensive guide to switching carriers if you’re looking for more insight on how to navigate the process.

Tech.title: People’s Picks: 4 Phone Brands Dominate, but 1 Reigns Supreme and It’s Not Apple
Tech.content:
Every few years, you may think about upgrading your smartphone. A lot of thought and research goes into your next choice, whether it’s the price, features or brand reputation. Maybe you’re eyeing the latest and greatest, or considering a different phone brand or model altogether. Our readers’ opinions may help you decide.

CNET’s People’s Picks dives into what our readers really think about their tech devices and services, like their internet service provider, TVs and even their mobile carrier.

This round was all about readers’ phone brands, just in time for Apple’s Sept. 9 Surprise and shine event, where we expect new iPhone models to be revealed. We asked about everything from brand loyalty to battery life, durability and even price-to-value. The results came down to four big-name tech brands. While there’s only one overall winner, other brands win in key categories that can make a big difference in your day-to-day tasks if you’re upgrading soon.

Overall winner: Google

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Google is the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Picks for Phones. CNET averaged the scores across three categories to determine the overall satisfaction rating, which includes customer satisfaction, battery longevity and price-to-value.

Google wins with a score of 4.52 out of 5, while Motorola trails closely behind with 4.45.

“It’s no surprise to me that Google and Motorola scored top marks because both sell some of the most affordable phones that people can buy. Motorola’s Moto G series costs hundreds of dollars less than Apple’s cheapest iPhone,” said CNET’s Director of Content, Patrick Holland. “At $500, Google’s Pixel 10A is one of the best values that you can buy today, especially as phone prices spike due to the ongoing RAM shortage caused by AI and data centers. It just goes to show that in 2026, you can spend less than $500 and still have a great phone that lasts you years.”

On the other hand, Samsung and Apple trail behind with scores of 4.19 and 3.87, respectively. Both brands have evolved in the smartphone space with AI-powered features, upgraded cameras, and thinner phone designs, but fell short in this category.

“There are a few factors at play here, most notably that Google and Motorola ship a fraction of the phones that Samsung does — so Pixel and Razr buyers are a more devoted core of customers than the many who buy Galaxy phones,” said CNET Managing Editor of Mobile David Lumb. A Counterpoint Research report on phone shipments in the first quarter of 2026 noted that Google (3% of the US market) and Motorola (10%) combined accounted for half of Samsung’s market share (26%).

The other thing to remember is that Google sells mostly premium phones.



“Aside from the Pixel 10A as a midrange device. Motorola and Samsung have wider ranges of more affordable and cheap phones, so I’d guess there’s less consumer fondness at the lower end of the device price scale,” Lumb said.

Apple’s fourth-place spot is a tougher nut to crack. Perhaps consumers haven’t seen as many upgrades in successive years as they would like in new iPhones, or they’re miffed at the higher prices Apple’s phones sell for. What’s most likely the case, Lumb suggested, is that there are simply more people buying new iPhones. In the Counterpoint report above, Apple handsets accounted for 58% of all phones shipped in the US.

AI features

AI features like photo editing, live translation and AI-powered summaries are becoming the focal point for new smartphone models. But what matters more is how much you’ll use those built-in features. Google Pixel wins with 88% of its users saying their phone’s AI features are essential and occasionally useful.

“Out of the four brands, only one is a true AI company, and that’s Google. In fact, Google’s Gemini AI can run on phones from all four brands, including the iPhone via an app. The Gemini Assistant can be used on Motorola and Samsung phones,” said Holland.

Lumb added that Google has led the charge in both including and promoting AI features in its Pixel phones that people actually use, like Magic Eraser and live translation.

“Pixel owners have been using AI features for years, and combined with Google aggressively inserting its Gemini assistant throughout the phone, it makes sense that Samsung Galaxy owners would feel a lesser impact from AI.”

Samsung has made plenty of AI advancements, like a health assistant and browser upgrades, but it falls behind, with only 64% of its users saying the same. Apple and Motorola trail behind with 14% and 8% each. Most Motorola users say the phone lacked built-in tools or ignored them.



What few AI features are available on iPhones were introduced more recently, so it’s unsurprising that their owners wouldn’t consider them essential to daily use, Lumb said. While Gemini continues to evolve, Apple’s advanced AI Siri was delayed for years and will finally launch with the upcoming iOS 27.

Battery life

Ties with Motorola



For a phone’s battery to exceed expectations, it must last a day or more. Motorola and Google tie in this category, with 74% saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations by lasting a full day or longer without needing to be charged. Comparatively, Samsung and Apple fall behind, with only about half (52%) saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations, while others say they just meet expectations. Apple finishes last, with only 31% reporting the same for their iPhones’ batteries. Most said their phone needed to be charged midday.

“The number one factor for battery life is how you use your phone. And I think this result speaks volumes about how much iPhone owners are on their phones,” said Holland.

CNET’s phone battery testing found that Apple’s phones had the longest battery life, with OnePlus placing second and Motorola third. However, the test doesn’t account for how you use your phone specifically each day – everyone is different. If you’re hyper-connected and your default is scrolling through social media apps or streaming videos, even the best battery life won’t be enough for you, Holland said. “Thankfully, Google, Motorola and Samsung, along with Apple, have all increased the charging speeds on their handsets to at least make topping them off less of a pain point.”

Motorola

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Value

Motorola wins in price-to-value, with 82% of its readers saying it offers exceptional value by delivering more than its price suggests. Only 4% rate the brand as overpriced.

“Before Motorola brought back the Razr as a foldable phone, its most popular handsets were its Moto G line that start as low as $200 and top out at $350,” said Holland. “Motorola has deep, long-term relationships with phone carriers, which often sell these phones at a discount.”

Compared with other brands, 45% of Pixel owners say Google’s phone offers exceptional value, and 35% of Samsung users say the same.

The surprising fact is that Apple places fourth in this category, with 58% of iPhone users saying it’s overpriced. Only 12% find the phone’s value exceptional. However, many tech brands are raising prices due to the RAM shortage, which makes it tough to determine what’s worth the high cost.

“The only company that hasn’t raised prices on its phones this year is Apple. There’s a chance it might announce a price hike at its Sept. 9 event. The cheapest iPhone the company sells starts at $600. You can find incredible Android phones for less, like the Google Pixel 10A for $500,” said Holland.

Apple

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Durability

Choosing a phone that doesn’t shatter, crack or leave you with a broken camera can make a big difference when you need one to last a few years. Some phones are more durable than others. Apple wins this category with 78% of readers saying it’s highly durable against drops and daily use with minimal to no damage. The remaining 22% either deal with normal wear and minor scuffs over time, report their phone as fragile or always have a heavy-duty case to protect it.

Holland said that when Apple released the iPhone 12 in 2020, it was the first to have a flat, dense build with squared-off sides to increase durability. In the years following, Samsung followed suit, adopting a flat build for its Galaxy S and S Plus models, and Google implemented a similar design with its Pixel phones.

Google follows closely behind with 72% saying their Pixel smartphone is highly durable, while 28% say it’s moderately durable.

Not as many readers with a Motorola say the phone is highly durable (65%), but even fewer readers with a Samsung (58%) phone say the same. Samsung users say their foldable phone and screens are fragile and only moderately durable. Some readers criticize the brand for the phone’s fragility and susceptibility to damage from drops.

Brand retention and loyalty

Despite Apple falling short in several categories, 86% of Apple users said they’re extremely likely to buy the same brand next time.

“Apple’s most popular product is the iPhone, but its iPhone-only features like iMessage and FaceTime, not found on Android, that keep people tied in,” said Holland. “Also, if you want to learn about how to use your iPhone or get it fixed, you can go to the Apple Store and talk with an actual human – I think those retail stores are Apple’s secret weapon.”

Whereas 79% of Samsung owners share the same sentiment for the brand. Over half of Google Pixel owners (58%) would buy a Google phone again, but only 42% of people with Motorola phones would. Other Motorola owners are using competitor research to determine their next phone purchase.

Methodology

CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,107 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from July 1 to July 28, 2026.

Tech.title: How to Watch Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ Event Tomorrow
Tech.content:
Apple

It’s almost time. Apple is holding its next event, which the company is calling “Surprise and shine,” tomorrow. Historically, Apple has used its September event to announce new hardware, particularly the newest models of iPhones. That means we only have a few hours left see if Apple will unveil the rumored foldable iPhone.

You can catch the Apple event on Apple’s website, Apple TV, the Apple Developer app and the company’s YouTube channel on Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 10 a.m. PT (1 p.m. ET, 6 p.m. BST). We expect to hear from Apple’s incoming CEO, John Ternus, for the first time in his role after he took up the mantle on Sept. 1.

Here are a few things Apple could announce at the event.

A foldable iPhone

Whether Apple calls it the iPhone Fold, iPhone Ultra or the iPhone Flip, the company could show off a foldable iPhone at its September event. Leaks and supply chain reports suggest the foldable iPhone will be a squat, book-style foldable, similar to the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8.

This is a mock-up of what a possible iPhone Fold might look like, according to CNET designer Jeffrey Hazelwood. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

Those same leaks also suggest the price of the iPhone foldable could be between $2,000 and $2,500, which could price many people out. According to a CNET survey, US adults are only willing to spend an average of $781 on a foldable iPhone, which is less than the price of the base model iPhone 17 ($799).

Patrick Holland, CNET’s director of content, said that foldable phones remain a niche interest among most shoppers, but that Apple is likely to price the device to reflect its expensive manufacturing costs.

New iPhone 18 Pro models

CNET’s Jeffrey Hazelwood created these custom renders of what an iPhone 18 Pro might look like. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

According to Bloomberg, Apple could unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max at its September event, too. Those iPhones could also see a price hike, with prices starting at $1,200, up from the iPhone 17 Pro‘s starting price of $1,100.

You might notice that entry-level iPhone 18 models are missing from that lineup. That’s because Bloomberg suspects Apple will split the iPhone launch this year. That means we could see the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September before Apple rolls out the iPhone 18, iPhone 18E and potentially a refreshed iPhone Air in the spring.

New Apple Watches

The (from left to right) Apple Watch Ultra 3, Apple Watch Series 11 and Apple Watch SE 3. Apple could show new Apple Watches at its event in September. Carly Marsh/CNET

Apple is also reportedly preparing to announce an Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its September event. According to Bloomberg, the new watches could include faster chips and new health and fitness features. However, the new watches likely won’t receive a design change.

There’s no solid information about how much these watches will cost. However, Apple has raised a lot of hardware prices this year, so while the starting price of the Apple Watch 11 is $399, the Apple Watch 12 could cost more at launch.

The AirPods 5

The AirPods 4 (pictured) are a few years old now, so Apple could show AirPods 5 at the company’s September event. Apple/CNET

Bloomberg also reports that Apple could debut the AirPods 5 at the September event, releasing an updated version of the company’s entry-level headphones. Apple released the AirPods 4 almost two years ago, in 2024. Apple isn’t expected to show the rumored camera-equipped AirPods at the September event. We could see those later this year, or in 2027.

The AirPods 4 had a starting price of $129 at launch, but given Apple’s other price increases, the AirPods 5 could also see a higher starting price.

Apple did not immediately respond to CNET’s request to comment.

For more Apple news, here’s what to know about the new M6 Mac Mini and when you might be able to preorder an iPhone 18.

Tech.title: I Actually Really Like Xiaomi’s Folding iPhone Ultra Rival
Tech.content:
Xiaomi took the wraps off its new foldable phone at IFA in Berlin and while I could only see it on a stand behind glass at first, I later managed to actually get my hands on the thing and have a brief play. It’s a nice-feeling foldable with a passport-style foldable that I absolutely love. Problem is, it’s got some stiff competition from both Samsung and Apple.

According to most rumors, Apple will be unveiling its first folding iPhone, likely named the iPhone Ultra, at its event on Sept. 9. Those same rumors suggest that Apple’s foldable will also have a passport-style design that’s short and squat when closed but opens out into a wider format that’s great for watching videos.

Xiaomi’s foldable next to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Xiaomi’s is a little smaller. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Neither are the first to the game; Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 launched earlier in the summer sporting a passport-style design that CNET’s Abrar Al-Heeti liked enough to give a CNET Editors’ Choice award to. Xiaomi’s phone is in a similar vein to Samsung’s. It’s squat, with a 5.38-inch outer display that unfolds to reveal a 7.58-inch inner display. I agree totally with Abrar when she said that this form factor is “refreshing” and “fun.”

The inner display looked bright and vibrant (at least, under the dim overhead office lights of my demo room) and the crease was barely noticeable. I recently reviewed Samsung’s book-style folding Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and I prefer the more passport style for its wider aspect ratio inner display. It just feels more natural.

You can prop it open like this. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Xiaomi says its custom hinge uses a “three-link” design for added strength and durability. I honestly can’t speak to that in my brief hands on time but it did feel satisfying to open, with it also being able to hold its position so you can half open it and prop it open.

It’s the first phone the company has released using its own in-house XRing 03 processor, which Xiaomi claims is as powerful as any other flagship chip right now — presumably including the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Elite found in Samsung’s Galaxy phones. It’s an interesting move to see the company build its own silicon from scratch. Both Apple and Google have done similar things and clearly Xiaomi agrees this is the way to have better control of all aspects of the product. How it performs on benchmarks remains to be seen.

I love that red color. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Other specs include a 200 megapixel main camera along with a 50 megapixel telephoto camera and a 6,000mAh silicon carbon battery. Solid specs, for sure, but I’ll have to reserve judgement on how these perform for when I get a model in my hands for some real testing.

But I’m impressed by the Xiaomi 18 Fold. It feels like one of the most sophisticated foldables the company has produced and I find that passport format much more intriguing than the more typical book- or flip-style of its previous foldables.

The wider format when open gives more space for videos. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Xiaomi has yet to say whether the phone will go on sale outside of mainland China, but I really hope it does. Xiaomi doesn’t officially sell any of its phones in the US, so don’t expect it there at any point, but I’ll keep my tea-stained British fingers crossed that I get a model at some point.

Editors’ note: Andrew Lanxon’s travel costs for the IFA conference were covered by Xiaomi. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Tech.title: We Rated the Weird Tech at IFA 2026 to Find the Wackiest Products
Tech.content:
Thousands of products crowded the halls of IFA 2026, one of the world’s largest consumer technology shows. Most promised to make our lives easier, healthier or more connected. A few appeared to receive a slightly different assignment — make something so strange that even a room full of jaded tech reporters would stop and stare.

After nearly a week on the show floor, we found tofu machines, pet phones, toothbrush cameras, AI companions and a rugged laptop that wants to be left in the sun. Some were surprisingly clever. Others raised questions nobody had previously thought to ask.

These are the weirdest products we spotted at IFA 2026, along with our entirely scientific assessment of whether they’re too weird to work.

Govee’s mood-reading skylight

Govee’s giant mood light was on display at IFA. David Watsky/CNET

Govee has long been at the forefront of strange home lighting creations, from literal curtains of light to spread across your garage to table lamps that look more like alien artifacts. Now Govee is showing off one of its oddest products yet: a dome-like ceiling light designed to mimic the sky and be “mood-responsive.”

In this case, mood-responsive means you can use Govee’s AI to talk about your mood or how you’re feeling, and the Govee app will suggest ceiling light color schemes to match. But the light can also create a specific blue wavelength designed to evoke blue skies and natural daylight.

Too weird to work? Not as weird as you may think. I’ve tested Govee’s AI before, and you really can generate lighting patterns based on your mood or random musings. But Govee already has so many lighting scenes in its app that I didn’t find it very practical — though definitely fun. I wonder how well it will work with a full ceiling light.

A gigantic tofu maker

The Nuvell plant protein maker is about the size of an espresso machine. David Watsky/CNET

If your two problems are not eating enough plant protein and having too much counter space, the Nuvell is here. This massive bean cooker and compressor is the size of an espresso machine and churns out blocks of tofu in as little as 30 minutes. It can make other vegan proteins depending on the legume you stick inside.

Plant protein made in the comfort of your kitchen. David Watsky/CNET

I asked the rep on duty whether the Nuvell could make cheese if you poured cow’s milk in. She claimed it could, but didn’t seem too confident.

Too weird to work? While it wasn’t operational at IFA, we assume the Nuvell does what it’s supposed to, since turning soybeans into tofu isn’t rocket science. The real question is whether it’s worth the space on your counter for this one-trick pony of a kitchen appliance.

A toothbrush with a built-in camera

A camera on your toothbrush is definitely a design choice. Dyson

Unless you’re a dentist, you probably don’t want a closer look at your teeth — but one intrepid brand came to IFA bearing a toothbrush that gets personal by using a built-in camera.

The Dyson Camerajet uses a camera with “Gap Optical Targeting.” Fortunately, you don’t have to personally review the 28 images per second the camera can take. Instead, an AI analyzes it for you and targets interdental gaps. From what we can tell, you can then aim the toothbrush’s jet of water at tooth gaps to make sure they get extra clean.

If you do want to play dentist like this, it’ll cost a sweet $500 for the advance.

Too weird to work? I’m calling this one too weird for sure. Price aside, you have to stand with your toothbrush in hand while holding your phone in the other to look at an enormous close-up of your teeth on the screen, then simultaneously brush and use the water flosser at the right angles to hit what look like gaps. The whole thing appears entirely unnecessary if you simply practice good brushing and flossing.

A tiny robot vacuum… for your bed

Yep — a whole robot vacuum, just for the bed. Creatulize

Creatulize came to IFA to show off the smallest robot vacuum in all of Berlin. The X1 Pro is the brand’s second-gen bed robot vacuum, designed to clean your bedding and mattress.

Using precision mode, the vac moves slowly and steadily across a mattress, sucking up dust, mites, hair and whatever else lurks. It can clean a king-size in about 20 minutes and has an easy-to-empty debris canister. Special sensors keep it from tumbling off the bed. When it hits an edge, it stops, turns and keeps on keepin’ on.

That’s one itty-bitty robot vac. David Watsky/CNET

Too weird to work? Mattress vacuums are becoming a thing, based on the idea that dirty mattresses exacerbate allergies. Nobody wants a dusty mattress, but whether or not you need a dedicated vacuum for it is up for debate. We’ll be testing the X1 Pro to find out.

An air conditioner trained to follow you

Midea’s new voice-controlled air conditioner follows you around the room with a stream of cool. David Watsky/CNET

One of the highlights we saw – and felt – was an air conditioner unit that sends custom cool air to you wherever you are. Midea’s new system uses spatial imaging and sensors to track your position in the room and deliver a stream of cool air your way. That means a cooler you and less energy wasted.

Midea’s smart AC works with the brand’s other air-quality appliances, including the humidifier. The two work in harmony through Midea’s smart sync to keep your home’s air at your desired temperature and humidity, no matter what Mother Nature has planned.

It’s also voice-activated, so you can turn it on or off, or activate the “mmWave sensor system” without getting up or even opening your phone.

Too weird to work? While the AC wasn’t officially up and running at IFA, Dyson launched a similar freestanding fan and air purifier that tracks humans in the room and spits fresh, cool air their way. We’re still testing that one in our lab, but would be surprised if the technology doesn’t live up to at least some of its promise.

SwitchBot’s AI shirt pin, the MindClip

SwitchBot’s AI clip sort of… spies on everyone around you. SwitchBot

If you thought AI was already in everything, just wait: SwitchBot is announcing the launch of its AI shirt device, the MindClip, at IFA. It’s made to clip onto your shirt pocket, collar, nearby strap or even belt. Once in place, it, well, essentially listens to everything that happens within a 3-meter radius for up to 20 hours and saves it for you.

The MindClip can recognize people by their voices and summarize conversations or events, ostensibly to help you with planning after a busy day. As far as AI goes, it’s no spying Meta glasses, but it is fairly invasive, especially for strangers you may be chatting with.

Too weird to work? This isn’t the first time we’ve seen an AI pin, although it is the smallest and least distracting version I’ve spotted. The problem is that none of them really took off, and some companies even pivoted to an entirely different product. So yes, it’s too weird to work for now, but maybe the rumored AI capabilities in Apple’s AirPods will be an exception.

The AI-powered companion doll from Lovense

Lovense’s updated AI companion doll also made an appearance at IFA. Lovense

Singaporean intimacy and sex toy company Lovense has brought the latest version of its AI “companion doll” to IFA, aiming to make it more lifelike than ever before. In addition to talking, remembering past facts and adjusting its personality, the silicone doll can blink, smile and look when called by its custom name. Users can also chat with the doll at a distance via a phone app and set up roleplay scenarios, if they prefer.

Too weird to work? Yes, the age of AI sex dolls is here. But it’s such an eclectic — and expensive (between $4,000 and $8,000) — proposition, this one is only for those with very specific tastes and a, ahh, particular relationship with AI. For others, Lovense also debuted several more conventional, AI-free toys.

A Eufy sensor that asks if you fell down

Eufy’s new sensor has a very, very specific purpose in the home. Eufy

When today’s home sensors can do nearly anything from recognizing when dogs bark to knowing when someone is tampering with a mailbox, it may sound strange to make a sensor specifically to say, “Oops, it looks like you fell down!” But that’s just what Anker’s Eufy brand has done.

There’s method behind this madness. The wall sensor uses a combo of algorithms and presence sensing with mmWave technology, no cameras necessary. It’s made to help those aging in place or living in rest homes without creating privacy concerns. The sensor even supports two-way audio, so family members or nurses can check in if they get an alert about a potential fall.

Quick note: As Anker consolidates its brand names, Eufy products are staying with us, but the Eufy name may not be around forever, so keep that in mind when shopping.

Too weird to work? In this case, not at all. I’ve already seen mmWave technology tap into Wi-Fi signals to help those aging in place, although Eufy’s sensor is the first I’ve seen that focuses on falls and enables two-way audio for a quick checkup. It’s a strong use of the technology.

Best DIY Home Security Systems of 2026: Install Them Yourself Dodge installation fees and take security into your own hands with these super smart security kits.

A smartphone for your pet

The Petphone certainly makes a lot of claims about AI pet powers. Petpogo

Ucloudlink has brought the newest version of its award-winning PetPhone to IFA this year, showing a world where cats and dogs have their own smartphone, too. Sort of.

The Petpogo PetPhone is technically a smart pet collar, and we’ve reviewed many of those. But this version comes with two-way audio to talk to your pet with an app and AI features that interpret behavior and motion so pets can theoretically initiate a call themselves, as well as emotion analysis of barks, meows and other actions. It also supports more traditional capabilities like tracking and geofencing, and it alerts pet parents to out-of-routine behaviors.

Too weird to work? No AI features can accurately interpret specific barks or meows into moods and feelings. That’s (currently) nonsense. And trying to get your pet to “call” you with specific behaviors sounds dubious at best. So most of the innovations here are too weird, but the underlying collar functionality looks usable.

These headphones that turn into a Bluetooth speaker

TDM’s Bluetooth speaker headphone hybrid is confusing. TDM

TDM is showing off its unique Neo headphones, with a literal twist. In normal mode, they look like a typical pair of wireless headphones. But twist and collapse the earcups, and they form into a small Bluetooth speaker with up to 8 hours of music playback. The dual-device comes with an aux port, a USB-C charging port and a carrying case.

Too weird to work? When was the last time you saw someone with headphones and thought, “What a pleasant, private music experience that person is having, I wish there was a way for them to share it with all the people nearby?” Nope. No one likes it when you play music out loud in public spaces, especially when the same device could let you listen privately. I’m calling these headphones too weird to work.

A soundwave-creating smart bed

Amada’s acoustic mattress claims many different applications. Amada

Amada brought a fascinating mattress to IFA called the Soundwave Smart Mattress. Yes, it connects to a phone app. And yes, it really does produce sound waves or at least a “vibroacoustic experience” with vibration modes for presleep relaxation, meditation, focus and recharging. I’m not sure how vibration is supposed to help with those things, but CNET health expert Anna Gragert told me vibration therapy does have applications for recovery and disease treatment. The bed is made of polyurethane foam and polyester fabric, with a four-pin power connector.

Too weird to work? Well, Magic Fingers did have their day in hotel rooms across the US, but that day ended pretty fast. I don’t know if a bed with good vibrations is what the average home is looking for, but if you’ve tried it and it works for you, this could be a shakingly good upgrade.

This 8-pound laptop wants to photosynthesize

Oukitel covered the RG14-P’s lid in solar panels because, apparently, outlets are optional now. Oukitel

Normally, leaving a laptop baking in direct sunlight is a terrible idea. The Oukitel RG14-P treats it like a charging strategy instead. Nearly the entire back of its display is covered in solar panels, which Oukitel says can recharge its 95-watt-hour battery to 50% in about 6 hours under ideal sunlight.

The rugged Windows laptop also has a 14.1-inch touchscreen and a dual-battery system with a removable pack. It weighs roughly 8.1 pounds, however, so carrying it into the wilderness may require the sort of person who was already shopping for a solar-powered industrial laptop.

Too weird to work? Not really. Six hours of perfect sunlight for half a charge won’t replace a wall outlet, but it could keep the laptop alive during fieldwork or an off-grid emergency. It’s less “solar MacBook” and more computer for someone whose office occasionally lacks walls.

Editor’s note: David Watsky’s travel costs for the IFA conference were covered by IFA. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own

Tech.title: The Best of IFA 2026: An Instant Pot for Cats, Camera-Equipped Toothbrush and More
Tech.content:
After nearly a week roaming the halls of IFA 2026, CNET staffers have seen a lot: some genuinely useful, some wonderfully strange. That includes a dishwasher and toothbrush equipped with cameras, Dyson’s largest air purifier and a speaker designed to soothe you to sleep. Together, they offer a glimpse at how tech companies think we’ll live, breathe, clean, sleep, work and play next.

Now that the show is wrapping up, we’ve sorted through everything we saw to pick the standouts. Here’s the best tech we spotted at IFA 2026.

An all-seeing dishwasher

Miele’s Diamond G8 isn’t your average dishwasher. David Watsky/CNET

Miele’s new Diamond G8 dishwasher has an AI-powered internal camera that scans your dishes and decides how to wash them so it doesn’t miss a single spot. Though Home and Kitchen Managing Editor David Watsky, who saw the dishwasher in person, was skeptical about this feature, he was left impressed.

But the Diamond G8’s scrubbing smarts don’t stop there. If you want the Diamond G8 to run only when electricity is most affordable, it can do that, too, waiting for the hours when power costs less.

Note-taking earbuds

Plaud One: your AI note-taking assistant earbuds. Plaud/CNET

Going beyond its AI note-taking wearable pin and credit card-like device that you can attach to your phone, Plaud launched the Plaud One earbuds to capture and transcribe your conversations and calls. You can even talk to Plaud’s AI by saying, “Hey Plaud,” and then ask it your questions or give it directives.

“We’d always recommend informing people that you’re using a recording device, and it’s important to note that recording phone calls without permission from all participants can be illegal in some states,” principal writer Katie Collins wrote when covering the Plaud One announcement.

A robot vacuum that seals itself to carpet

The Roomba Max 875 Combo is all about clean carpet. iRobot

While robot vacuums are great for taking the effort out of keeping your floors clean, CNET’s testing has found that they don’t offer the same suction power as traditional vacuums. iRobot aims to improve on that with its new Roomba Max 875 Combo, which uses SealForce technology to seal itself to carpet and better suction up spots that need extra cleaning.

In a video call with Home and Robotics Editor Ajay Kumar prior to IFA 2026, Adam Pope, vice president and chief engineer at iRobot, said SealForce is like pressing harder with a traditional vacuum to thoroughly clean a specific patch of carpet, but in a robot vacuum format.

A smart ring puts contactless payments at your fingertips

Imagine how cool it will feel to use your ring for contactless payments. Circular

In addition to having the health-tracking capabilities we expect of smart rings, Circular has added contactless payments, a feature typically found on smartwatches and smartphones, to its new subscription-free Ring 3 Pro and Ring 3 Slim. When covering the launch, principal writer Vanessa Hand Orellana wrote that the company also gave both rings haptic vibration alerts, a feature previously available on its first Circular Ring, along with advanced sleep metrics, glucose trend estimates and access to its AI health coach.

A laptop built to be repaired

The Vero 16 comes with its own repair guide. Acer/CNET

With its new fourth-generation Vero 16, Acer brings the “right to repair” conversation into focus, as CNET writer Tyler Graham explained that the modular laptop is designed to let users easily upgrade its components themselves. There’s even a repair guide engraved on it to help with these swaps.

The Vero 16 didn’t come alone, as it was announced alongside Acer’s compact 14-inch Swift Blade 14 and sleek 16-inch Swift Air 16.

A speaker that lulls you to sleep

Sleep has never sounded so sweet. Katie Collins/CNET

Alongside its Sleep Earbuds 4 and Sleep Earbuds 4 Pro with a touchscreen case, Anker introduced the SleepLab Pro speaker, which uses radar to track your sleep, breathing and heart rate, then customizes its audio to help you drift off to dreamland and stay there. “It looks like a thoughtfully designed piece of kit that I know I’d be happy to have on my bedside table,” Collins wrote when describing the device. It also triples as a sunrise alarm clock and a nightlight that glows in a range of shades.

A non-Pro SleepLab has the same features, minus radar sleep tracking.

Dyson’s largest air purifier

Air purifier or Dune sandworm? You decide. Dyson

The new Dyson HushJet Big+Quiet Cool Pure+Formaldehyde (try to say that five times fast) was designed to purify multiple rooms using the company’s most powerful processor. As Kumar put it, it looks like a Dune sandworm with its nozzle head that can be rotated and tilted. While operating quietly, the purifier can capture 99.99% of pollutants down to 0.01 microns for a breath of fresh air.

Lenovo’s first rollable work laptop

Lenovo is on a roll. Josh Goldman/CNET

Lenovo’s Project Swan concept is a laptop that expands horizontally at the touch of a button, transforming its display from 14 to 17 inches. But unlike the Legion Pro Rollable Graham spotted at CES 2026, this isn’t a gaming laptop – it’s for work. Perfect for work trips when you want a more compact 14-inch display for travel, but a 17-inch for getting the job done (or watching movies during your downtime).

Dyson’s first toothbrush

Plaque begone! Tara Brown/CNET

Dubbed the CameraJet, Dyson’s first toothbrush has a built-in, AI-powered camera that detects gaps between your teeth within 100 milliseconds so that it can floss while you brush. To do so, the brush has an anti-gravity tank that its charging dock fills with mouthrinse, which its jet uses to floss.

You can even use the CameraJet’s camera as an endoscope to see your teeth in the app, where brushing and flossing insights, coverage maps and guided cleaning are also available. However, this high-tech toothbrush comes at a cost: $500.

An Instant Pot-like feeder for cats

Get your cat to stop meowing at you for food, and let them meow at this machine instead. David Watsky/CNET

Pet care and home cleaning company Neakasa showed off its Riko smart wet food maker, which Watsky described as an Instant Pot for cats. All you have to do is add water to Riko’s reservoir and freeze-dried food, so refrigeration isn’t required. On demand or when feeding time is scheduled in the app, the device will prepare your feline’s feast by rehydrating and mixing the cat food. Bon appetit!

A mom Roomba carrying its baby

One happy Roomba family. Ajay Kumar/CNET

Kumar, who covers robot vacuums for CNET and has seen all there is to see with these cleaning devices, was genuinely surprised when he set his sights on iRobot’s Roomba Duo. While it’s currently just a concept, the Duo has an egg-like mothership module with a floor washer and steamer and a mechanical arm that carries and deploys a slimmer baby Roomba to get under furniture and clean narrow spaces its larger mother module can’t reach. A true dynamic duo.

A smart radiator valve

Its high-res screen shows temperature, settings and device status in real time. Sonoff

Home Security and Smart Home Senior Editor Tyler Lacoma has been waiting for a smart thermostat that isn’t just for forced air heating and cooling, and smart home company Sonoff displayed exactly that at IFA. The TRV Smart Thermostatic Radiator Valve provides three temperature scheduling plans and frost protection and anti-calcification reminders. It even connects to window sensors to prevent energy waste. Just screw it onto your radiator’s valve pipe and let it take care of the rest.

A Roomba that carries another Roomba

The Roomba Duo deploys a smaller robot to clean the places its enormous parent cannot. iRobot

Apparently, one Roomba is no longer enough. The Roomba Duo is a concept floor-cleaning system consisting of a large robot that vacuums and steam-mops open areas and a smaller Roomba that rides on top of it. When the Duo encounters furniture or another space it can’t squeeze beneath, a mechanical arm lowers the little robot to the floor and sends it in.

The two robots share a map and coordinate their cleaning through the Roomba app, while the larger unit also carries clean and dirty water tanks, a dust bag and enough hardware to function as its own mobile dock. It’s ambitious and ridiculous-looking, but honestly, it’s exactly the sort of thing we come to IFA to see. Because it remains a concept, iRobot hasn’t announced a price or release date.

IFA runs from Sept. 4 to Sept. 8. We’ll continue updating this list as we see the best that the tech event has to offer.

Tech.title: 2027 Android Phones Could Boost Gaming Graphics and AI Tasks With Arm’s New Chip Tech
Tech.content:
Arm debuted its new CSS for Mobile 2 technology for chipmakers to include on future silicon powering smartphones. The primary upgrade is around the GPU, which has been redesigned to allow AI to upscale graphics and improve the framerate for a better mobile gaming experience on premium Android phones coming next year. Arm has also improved its CPU clusters for AI agent processing.

Every smartphone needs a CPU and GPU, but more processing power is needed at the top end of the phone market. Phones using MediaTek chips often have Arm CPU cores and GPUs, with last year’s Oppo Find X9 Pro packing a MediaTek Dimensity 9500 chip that uses a Mali G1-Ultra GPU to render graphics.

Now, Arm is announcing the Mali G2-Ultra NX, which the company says is its first AI-native GPU, using AI to improve rendered visuals directly in the graphics pipeline, lowering latency and improving power efficiency. Typically, graphics data is ported to and from other AI-dedicated areas, such as the neural processing unit, to enable AI acceleration, but integrating this directly into the GPU reduces travel time and energy used.

The Mali G2-Ultra uses a trio of AI methods to perform this. Neural super sampling turns low-resolution renders into higher-resolution images with Arm, suggesting a jump from 540p to 1080p, while neural frame rate upscaling generates frames between rendered ones — for example, to jump from 30 frames per second to 60. Neural super sampling and denoising takes the former technology and scrubs out “noise” (dot artifacts in an image) for graphically demanding scenes like ray-traced reflections and complex lighting.

By having the phone render graphics in lower resolution and fewer frames that can be boosted with AI, smartphones can be made smaller and potentially cheaper, said Chris Bergey, executive vice president of Arm’s Edge AI Business unit.

“If we can provide an amazing 540p, 30 frames per second experience, and it allows you to use a smaller battery, that allows for a smaller form factor and potentially allows for a lower-cost handheld,” Bergey said.

During a briefing ahead of the announcement, Arm showed off a game it co-developed with Sumo Digital to showcase those AI methods. Amid scenes of a fantasy character descending into a cave system illuminated by neon-bright giant mushrooms, Arm explained that the game was a proof of concept for how developers could use the AI methods to deliver 4x higher performance efficiency and up to 70% lower external memory traffic (e.g. data transferring out from and back to the GPU) compared with conventional graphics rendering.

All these improvements lead to a 24% improvement in benchmark performance along with a 14% improvement in ray tracing.

CPU core upgrades for AI agent tasks

Arm announced new C2 CPU cores designed for AI agent workflows on devices. Compared to last year’s C1 cores, the new C2 cores have up to 15% higher single-thread and 12% higher multi-thread performance and 1.7x performance across AI models while using 38% less power. They also launch apps and browse the web faster.

Higher single-thread performance reduces latency, while multi-thread performance helps multiple tasks progress concurrently, Arm explained in a press release. Across a sample agentic workflow combining several tasks — speech processing, memory retrieval, reasoning, application execution and web browsing — C2-ultra cores completed the workflow 24% faster than last year’s cores.

Each chipmaker decides the type and number of cores to include in their system-on-chip, balancing performance, efficiency and cost. The aforementioned MediaTek Dimensity 9500, released last year, has an eight-core CPU: one C1-Ultra, three C1-Premium and four C1-Pro.

Tech.title: Hypershell’s Halo Full-Leg Exoskeleton Made Me Dream Big About the Hikes I Hope to One Day Attempt
Tech.content:
Do you consider yourself fit and healthy? I strength train, run, hike, climb and swim — albeit not according to any kind of training plan or schedule — and yet there are so many ways my body struggles on a daily basis.

Even people who consider themselves to have a high level of cardiovascular fitness might lack strength, balance or flexibility. It’s almost impossible for one person to adhere to a truly holistic training plan. We all have weaknesses. We all know what it’s like to feel fatigued.

What if technology could pick up the slack? That’s the premise behind the Hypershell Halo, a full-leg exoskeleton unveiled at IFA in Berlin last week. This is far from the first Hypershell exoskeleton, but unlike previous models, the Halo extends further down the leg to provide support through the knee and calf, as well as through the thigh and hip.

The Hypershell Halo is flexible enough to allow a full range of movement. Katie Collins/CNET

The Hypershell unified architecture is one carbon-fiber, load-bearing structure with what the company is calling a “fish-spine adaptive joint” to allow for flexibility through the hip and into the leg. Its four-motor system is designed to power you through a whole range of movements while reducing knee-muscle fatigue by up to 40% across all types of terrain.

As someone with chronically creaky knees, I was excited to try the Hypershell Halo over the weekend at IFA. The target audience for an exoskeleton may be older adults and people with limited mobility, but Hypershell seems to be hoping the Halo will have broader appeal. Someone like me, who is active and enthusiastic about exploring the outdoors, but who sometimes reaches their physical limits earlier than they’d like, is also a contender.

I quickly discovered that putting the Hypershell Halo on is all part of the adventure. One belt attaches around the waist, and two flexible straps feed around the thighs. It takes a good few minutes and help from two people to adjust the exoskeleton to fit my proportions, but once the settings are right, it’s very quick to take on and off. (In an on-stage demonstration during the Halo launch event, I watched as the presenter put the exoskeleton on in just 16 seconds.)

My first impression is that I feel a little stiff and restricted, but that sensation immediately evaporates once I start moving. The kit weighs 2.6kg in total, with the majority of that distributed around my waist. I thought the Halo would take some getting used to and might disrupt my natural gait, but it doesn’t at all. Instead, I instantly feel lighter in my natural movements. Squatting and standing from a low seated position without using my hands for support and thrust is totally effortless.

Most of the weight is distributed around your waist. Katie Collins/CNET

As I trample cheerfully all over Hypershell’s multistory booth, I find that that the only pressure anywhere in my legs is in my ankle joints. Going downstairs, I feel none of the usual pressure in my knees, thanks to the cushioning effect. The exoskeleton isn’t doing the work of walking for me, but it feels as though I could keep going for much longer.

This is one of the main use cases Hypershell is putting forward. Avid runners and hikers could potentially do far more than they’re used to without tiring. The Halo supports speeds of up to 17km per hour, which is a 2.5-hour marathon pace. Given that that’s the same as my half-marathon pace, I’d be interested to see what I could achieve while running in the Halo.

As I descend the stairs, thinking about how difficult it usually is walking down the side of a mountain — just one long exercise in trying not to fall — I wonder whether the Halo could allow me to attempt some of the more challenging and vertiginous hikes I’m drawn to, but currently find too intimidating. I have my eye on a multiday Iceland trek, some steep summits in Lofoten and a whole bunch of routes in Patagonia. It also occurs to me that the Halo could be useful for groups with uneven levels of fitness or walking speeds. Could it be responsible for helping couples dodge the infamous alpine divorce? Or is that just delaying the inevitable?

For longer hikes, the battery supports up to 20 hours of use and can be easily swapped out. It only 370g, meaning it shouldn’t be too much of a burden to carry a spare or two.

I briefly switch the Halo to fitness mode, which increases the resistance for people who enjoy the feeling of physically working harder. I get the logic behind it, but I’m not one of these people I ask for it to be turned off again almost immediately. I guess it’s good that it exists for those who want it, but it’s not what I need after multiple days at a trade show.

One of the most interesting aspects of the Halo is how it uses AI. Over 30 sensors continuously capture lower-body movement, feeding data into the on-board AI chip, which can predict how you’re going to move 200ms before you actually do. This predictive technology means the Halo is adapting in real time to your activity, supporting your every move as you make it.

It can’t tell that this is happening while I’m wearing the exoskeleton, but I also suspect that that means it’s working as it should. After all, AI is the kind of technology that’s largely invisible when it’s at its most effective.

Perhaps the only drawback of wearing the Hypershell Halo is that it’s not subtle, and exoskeletons are still rare enough that it will likely attract attention if you wear one in public. If that doesn’t deter you and you’re ready to embrace life as cyborg in the here and now, the Hypershell Halo is available for preorder immediately, priced at $2,299.

Editors’ note: Katie Collins’ travel costs for the IFA conference were covered in part by Xiaomi. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.
